Description: The dollar rose against a basket of major currencies on Monday on traders' bets that China and the United States are moving closer to a trade deal that would end sparring between the world's two biggest economies.

Headlines: Legal expert Dagmar Valcarcel to join Deutsche Bank's supervisory board: report
Description: Dagmar Valcarcel, a legal expert, will join Deutsche Bank's supervisory board, German newspaper Handelsblatt said on Wednesday without naming its sources.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank denies report it prevented Trump transactions being flagged
Description: Deutsche Bank denied a report that said some of its executives rejected the advice of the bank's own anti-money laundering specialists and prevented some transactions involving entities controlled by President Donald Trump and his son-in-law, Jared Kushner, being filed with the government.

Headlines: Philip Morris sues South Korea over e-cigarette info disclosure
Description: Philip Morris Korea Inc. said on Monday it has filed a lawsuit against the South Korean government, demanding the disclosure of information on a recent test that concluded electronic cigarettes contain harmful substances.

Headlines: Renault chairman hopes decision on new CEO is made 'in coming days'
Description: Renault  Chairman Jean-Dominique Senard said Wednesday he hoped the decision on the French carmaker's new CEO would be made in "the coming days".

Headlines: Goldman Sachs UK unit reports gender pay gap of 51 percent
Description: Goldman Sachs's British business on average paid women 51 percent less than men per hour in 2018, the U.S. investment bank said on Monday, down from 56 percent the year before.

Headlines: Nokia sells digital health venture, executive to leave
Description: Nokia said on Thursday it had sold its small digital health business, including activity trackers and smartwatches, and the executive who wound down the company's consumer ventures will leave Nokia after less than a year in the job.

Headlines: PG&E says equipment probably caused deadly Camp Fire
Description: PG&E Corp, which filed for bankruptcy last month because of potential liabilities from wildfires in California, said it is probable that its equipment will be determined to be an "ignition point" of the 2018 Camp Fire.

Headlines: Alaska warned U.S. government its largest regional airline was on verge of collapse: letter
Description: Alaska's congressional delegation warned U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin last week that many of its airlines, including its largest regional carrier, RavnAir Group, were on the verge of collapse, according to a letter seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Fed's Bostic: Business 'getting nervous again' as virus surges
Description: The surge in U.S. coronavirus cases has made business owners "nervous again," Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank President Raphael Bostic said on Tuesday, and prompted him to focus on company decisions over the next three to six weeks.

Headlines: Worsening Italian crisis batters stock markets
Description: A spiraling Italian political crisis provoked a global stock market sell-off on Tuesday, cut the euro to a 10-month low and spiked borrowing costs for the government in Rome.

Headlines: Wall Street Week Ahead: Investors look for buys as virus fears crush travel stocks
Description: Bargain-hunting investors are eyeing the shares of airlines, hotels, cruise lines and other companies that have been among the worst-hit by the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: NMC in talks with lenders to avoid administration
Description: Troubled hospital group NMC Health  said on Monday it is in talks with Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank , seeking to convince it to withdraw an application that the lender had filed proposing that NMC be placed under administration.

Headlines: OPEC posts first 2019 oil-output rise despite Saudi cuts: Reuters survey
Description: OPEC oil output has risen in August for the first month this year as higher supply from Iraq and Nigeria outweighed restraint by top exporter Saudi Arabia and losses caused by U.S. sanctions on Iran, a Reuters survey found.

Headlines: Boeing addresses new 737 MAX software issue that could keep plane grounded longer
Description: Boeing Co  said on Friday it is addressing a new software issue discovered in Iowa last weekend during a technical review of the proposed update to the grounded Boeing 737 MAX, a development that could further delay the plane's return to service.

Headlines: Airbus bags new orders as delivery target doubts grow
Description: Airbus narrowed a sales gap against U.S. rival Boeing by finalising orders for 120 of the former Bombardier CSeries jet, but shares in Europe's top planemaker fell as doubts surfaced over a target for overall 2018 deliveries.

Headlines: Saudi energy minister calls for affordable energy supply at G20 meeting
Description: The Saudi energy minister told a conference of the G20 group of the world's largest economies on Friday that ensuring affordable energy supply is key to facilitating a global economic recovery.

Headlines: Stocks gain on U.S.-China trade hopes, dollar flat
Description: Global equity markets gained and the dollar held steady on Thursday ahead of the G20 summit where a scheduled meeting of U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping has stirred hopes that trade tensions could ease.

Headlines: Ryanair says not seeing any Brexit impact, well-prepared for no-deal
Description: Europe's biggest low cost airline Ryanair  is not seeing any impact from Brexit on demand for flights, and is prepared for a no-deal, chief marketing officer Kenny Jacobs said.

Headlines: Continental, Valeo seek EU antitrust action against Nokia
Description: German car parts maker Continental and French rival Valeo have joined Daimler and Bury Technologies to seek an EU antitrust investigation into Nokia's patent licensing practices for cars, the Finnish tech company said on Wednesday.

Headlines: AIG to sell 76.6% stake in Fortitude Re for $1.8 billion
Description: U.S. insurer American International Group Inc  said on Monday it would sell a major portion of its stake in reinsurer Fortitude Re to buyout fund Carlyle Group  and Japanese insurer T&D Holdings  for about $1.8 billion.

Headlines: Ex-Intel executive departs Google as chipmaker searches for CEO
Description: Diane Bryant, a former Intel Corp  executive who headed the chipmaker's data center unit, is leaving Alphabet Inc's  cloud computing unit less than a year after joining and just as her old employer searches for a new chief executive.

Headlines: Volvo expects electric car margins to match conventional vehicles by 2025
Description: Volvo Cars expects its margins on electric cars to match those of vehicles with combustion engines by 2025, the head of the Chinese-owned Swedish carmaker told Reuters.

Headlines: Ant Group listing would be fillip for Hong Kong's flagging IPO market
Description: An initial public offering from Alibaba's  Ant Group by year-end would give equity capital markets in Hong Kong a timely boost after a new security law cast in doubt the city's future as a global financial centre, analysts said on Thursday.

Headlines: U.S. panel to review how airplanes certified after Boeing 737 crashes
Description: The U.S. Transportation Department said on Monday that a new blue ribbon commission will review how the Federal Aviation Administration certifies new aircraft after two Boeing 737 MAX jets crashed in recent months, killing nearly 350 people.

Headlines: Algeria energy minister says OPEC+ countries to discuss 'substantial' oil output cuts
Description: Algeria energy minister and OPEC president said on Tuesday OPEC+ countries will discuss new "substantial" oil production cuts at their meetings in Vienna this week, Algerian state news agency APS reported.

Headlines: Low rates bruise Bank of America profits into 2020
Description: Bank of America Corp got stung by lower interest rates in the fourth quarter, sending its profit down 4%, a trend that management expects to continue this year.

Headlines: Exclusive: Behind Grindr's doomed hookup in China, a data misstep and scramble to make up
Description: Early last year, Grindr LLC's Chinese owner gave some Beijing-based engineers access to personal information of millions of Americans such as private messages and HIV status, according to eight former employees, prompting U.S. officials to ask it to sell the dating app for the gay community.

Headlines: Bezos buys Warner Estate in Beverly Hills for record $165 million
Description: Amazon Chief Executive Jeff Bezos, the world's wealthiest person, has purchased a Beverly Hills mansion known as the Warner Estate from media mogul David Geffen for $165 million, a source familiar with the deal said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Banks must step up climate risk disclosures, Lagarde says
Description: Banks must improve transparency on their exposure to climate- change risk and central banks need to pay closer attention as the entire financial sector is at risk, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said on Thursday.

Headlines: Timeline: Twists and turns in Mediaset vs Vivendi TV drama
Description: Italian broadcaster Mediaset  and shareholder Vivendi  were negotiating on Friday to find a way to end a three-year legal battle after all-night talks failed to produce a breakthrough, sources said.

Headlines: OPEC in the dark on oil supply as Russia, Iran cut exports
Description: OPEC is in the dark on the oil supply outlook for the second half of this year, with Iranian and Russian outages looking increasingly significant but Saudi Arabia reluctant to pump more due to fears of a price crash, sources in the organization said.

Headlines: Oil surges amid OPEC caution to offset Iran sanctions
Description: Oil prices hit their highest in about six months on Tuesday as sources said Gulf OPEC members were ready to raise output only if there was demand before offsetting any shortfall following a U.S. decision to end waivers for buyers of Iranian crude.

Headlines: Turkey, Volkswagen close in on production plant deal: sources
Description: Turkey is increasingly confident German carmaker Volkswagen  will build a production plant in the country after an "extremely positive" meeting between a senior company official and President Tayyip Erdogan this week, three Turkish sources said.

Headlines: VW, Ford team up on trucks, eye deals on EVs, self-driving cars
Description: Volkswagen AG  and Ford Motor Co  said on Tuesday they will join forces on commercial vans and pickups and are exploring joint development of electric and self-driving technology, actions meant to save the automakers billions of dollars.

Headlines: Walmart likely discriminated against female workers, U.S. agency says
Description: Walmart Inc likely discriminated against 178 female workers by paying them less, denying them promotions or both, because of their gender, the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission said in memos seen by Reuters.

Headlines: Renewed U.S.-China trade tensions push down Wall Street
Description: Wall Street's major indexes dipped on Wednesday as inflamed trade tensions between the United States and China weighed on investor sentiment.

Headlines: Proxy adviser ISS recommends against GE keeping auditor KPMG
Description: Proxy advisory firm Institutional Shareholder Services on Thursday recommended that shareholders of General Electric Co  vote against keeping accounting firm KPMG as the company's auditor because of "concerns about GE's previously undisclosed liabilities and accounting practices."

Headlines: Bombardier opening new California rail-car assembly site
Description: Canada's Bombardier is opening a new facility in California that will assemble rail cars for San Francisco's rapid transit system by year's end, and potentially serve other West Coast rail projects.

Headlines: Carmakers Dacia and Ford resume production in Romania
Description: Romanian carmaker Dacia, owned by France's Renault  and Ford Motor Co's  Craiova plant resumed operations on Monday after output was halted due to the coronavirus pandemic in March, they said.

Headlines: Q&A: Government coronavirus directives shield employers from bias, safety claims: MoFo partners
Description: The coronavirus pandemic is forcing employers to make tough decisions that could lead to legal liability, but most companies should be in the clear if they follow the advice of government authorities, according to Morrison & Foerster partners Janie Schulman and Christine Lyon.

Headlines: U.S. education groups McGraw-Hill, Cengage plan all-stock merger
Description: Educational publishers McGraw-Hill Education Inc and Cengage Learning Holdings II Inc are planning an all-stock merger, McGraw-Hill said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Uber offer for Grubhub fans worries over delivery fees charged to restaurants
Description: The possibility that Uber Technologies Inc , which runs Uber Eats, could acquire Grubhub Inc  is reigniting some restaurants' worries over the commissions charged to eateries by the third-party delivery companies.

Headlines: Oil rises slightly as OPEC+ complies with production cuts
Description: Oil prices rose slightly on Tuesday as OPEC and its allies cut production by more than agreed to in June, although demand concerns lingered due to increased cases of COVID-19 in the United States. Brent crude  futures settled up 18 cents at $42.90 a barrel, after moving lower earlier in the session. U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude  futures rose 19 cents to $40.29 a barrel.

Headlines: McDonald's warns of headaches in 2019 as overseas business booms
Description: McDonald's Corp warned higher labor costs, expenses for remodeling stores and a stronger dollar would weigh on its earnings in 2019, after a strong performance outside the United States powered better-than-expected fourth quarter results.

Headlines: Factbox: Boeing's changing schedule for 737 MAX fix, return to service
Description: Boeing Co said on Tuesday it does not expect to win approval for the return of the 737 MAX to service until mid-year due to further potential developments in the certification process and regulatory scrutiny on its flight control system.

Headlines: Oil up more than 1% on Mideast tensions and supply cuts
Description: Oil prices rose more than 1% on Monday, supported by Middle East tensions and OPEC-led supply cuts as well as continued crude disruptions from Russia after a contamination problem discovered last month.

Headlines: Uber, distracted backup driver cited by NTSB in fatal self-driving crash
Description: A U.S. safety agency on Tuesday faulted Uber for inadequate attention to safety and decisions in the company's autonomous vehicle development in an investigation into the first-ever death involving a self-driving vehicle, which also cited the vehicle's distracted back-up driver.

Headlines: Blackstone launches $5.5 billion F&R bridge loan
Description: LONDON (LPC) - Blackstone  has launched a  $5.5 billion bridge loan to support the pending bond issuance for its acquisition of a majority stake in Thomson Reuters’  Financial and Risk division (F&R), which is expected to complete later this year.

Headlines: Energy giants opening natural gas spigots, fueling profit rise
Description: The world's largest oil companies are pumping more natural gas than ever before, helping to spur a rise in profits while sating rising global demand for fuels that can mitigate global greenhouse gas emissions.

Headlines: Companies seen slashing capex 12% this year, deeper than in 2009: data
Description: Big and mid-cap firms globally are expected to slash capital spending by an average 12% this year as they reel from the fallout of lockdowns and other measures imposed to rein in the coronavirus pandemic, analysts' estimates show.

Headlines: Retail sector companies turn to masks, gloves in coronavirus fight
Description: Major U.S. retail sector companies on Thursday moved to allay health and safety concerns of staff working at warehouses and stores through the coronavirus pandemic by promising face masks, gloves and sanitizers.

Headlines: Toyota names new North America CEO as industry faces unprecedented shift
Description: Toyota Motor Corp  on Wednesday said its North America chief executive, Jim Lentz, would retire on April 1, and tasked the unit's chief operating officer, Tetsuo "Ted" Ogawa, with navigating an industry shift to electrification and automation.

Headlines: Boeing resumes 737 MAX production at low rate
Description: Boeing Co  on Wednesday said it has resumed production of its 737 MAX passenger jet at the company’s Renton, Washington, plant at a "low rate" after halting production in January following two crashes that killed 346 people.

Headlines: Steinhoff's U.S. unit Mattress Firm exits bankruptcy, shuts 660 stores
Description: Steinhoff International  said on Thursday its Mattress Firm Inc unit, the largest U.S. mattress retailer, emerged out of bankruptcy with access to $525 million in exit financing, within two months of filing for Chapter 11 protection.

Headlines: American Airlines pulls 737 MAX from schedule through April 6
Description: American Airlines Group Inc  will extend cancellations of Boeing Co  737 MAX flights through April 6, it said on Thursday, a day after the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration said it would not approve the plane's return to service before January.

Headlines: Exclusive: Investment firms fight to inject cash in Brazil carrier Oi
Description: Three distressed asset funds have sued for the right to participate in a 4 billion reais ($1 billion) capital increase for Brazilian telecom Oi SA  as part of its in-court restructuring, four sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters this week.

Headlines: French carmaker Renault names Luca de Meo as new CEO
Description: French carmaker Renault  on Tuesday named former Volkswagen's  Seat brand executive Luca de Meo as its new chief executive, as Renault moves to create a new management in the post-Ghosn era and shore up its alliance with Nissan .

Headlines: Deutsche Boerse chief says plans to fulfil his term as CEO
Description: Deutsche Boerse  Chief Executive Theodor Weimer said on Tuesday that he planned to complete his term through the end of 2024 at the helm of the stock exchange operator.

Headlines: Fiji suspends Boeing 737 MAX flights
Description: Fiji Airways and the Civil Aviation Authority of Fiji on Wednesday temporarily grounded the carrier's two Boeing Co 737 MAX planes, following two fatal crashes involving the aircraft in Indonesia and Ethiopia.

Headlines: Russian and Saudi energy ministers to meet at G20: RIA
Description: Russia's energy minister Alexander Novak will meet his Saudi counterpart at the G20 summit in Argentina and discuss an oil output reduction in 2019, RIA news agency cited Novak as saying on Friday.

Headlines: Mastercard to allow staff to work from home until virus fears subside
Description: Mastercard Inc  will not ask employees to return to its worldwide corporate offices until they are comfortable that the sometimes fatal coronavirus is under control with vaccines or other measures, a senior executive told Reuters on Wednesday.

Headlines: China welcomes any effort to move Huawei case toward resolution
Description: China's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday that Canada's arrest of Meng Wanzhou, a top executive with Chinese tech giant Huawei, was a mistake from the start, and welcomed any efforts to move the case toward a correct resolution.

Headlines: Trade uncertainty to trim $850 billion global output: Fed paper
Description: Trade policy uncertainty driven by the Trump administration's escalating dispute with China means hundreds of billions of dollars in lost U.S. output and as much as $850 billion lost globally through early next year, research published this week by the Federal Reserve suggests.

Headlines: Explainer: 'Stablecoins' in the spotlight as Facebook unveils Libra cryptocurrency
Description: The original cryptocurrency accounts for over half of the $285 billion global coin trading market. But that dominance is under threat, with a host of alternative digital coins emerging as developers race to build cryptocurrencies able to enter  mainstream commerce and finance.

Headlines: Fed's Evans expects virus impacts on economy to be short-lived
Description: The coronavirus outbreak will likely have only a "short-lived imprint" on the U.S. economy, Chicago Federal Reserve bank President Charles Evans said on Tuesday night.

Headlines: Buffett profits as venture in Canadian mortgage business ends
Description: Billionaire investor Warren Buffett is cutting ties with a  Canadian mortgage business after a nifty trade that provided the company with a potential lifeline.

Headlines: China's record trade surplus with U.S. adds fuel to trade war fire
Description: China's trade surplus with the United States widened to a record in August even as the country's export growth slowed slightly, an outcome that could push President Donald Trump to turn up the heat on Beijing in their cantankerous trade dispute.

Headlines: Roku tumbles 15% as Morgan Stanley warns of streaming 'exuberance'
Description: Roku Inc's high-flying stock tumbled 15% on Monday after Morgan Stanley downgraded the video streaming company, warning that revenue and profit growth could slow next year.

Headlines: Exclusive: U.S. firms may get nod to restart Huawei sales in two-four weeks - official
Description: The U.S. may approve licenses for companies to re-start new sales to Huawei in as little as two weeks, according to a senior U.S. official, in a sign President Donald Trump's recent effort to ease restrictions on the Chinese company could move forward quickly.

Headlines: Beyond Meat vs Zhenmeat: The battle for China's meatless market
Description: U.S. plant-based "meat" makers targeting China like Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat Inc will need to battle homegrown rivals which are developing local favorites such as dumplings and mooncakes to nab a share of the lucrative market.

Headlines: KKR earnings slide 23% as weaker deal activity hits revenue
Description: Private equity firm KKR & Co  reported a 23% year-on-year drop in its quarterly after-tax distributable profit on Tuesday, as fee revenue slid amid a broader slowdown in asset sales by buyout firms.

Headlines: Tesla's German shares fall after CEO Musk drops plan to take company private
Description: Germany-listed shares in Tesla  fell more than 3 percent in early deals on the Tradegate exchange on Monday, after Chief Executive Elon Musk called off his bid to take the company private.

Headlines: U.S. regulator sides with FCA in Jeep trade case against Mahindra
Description: A U.S. regulator ruled that India's Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd infringed upon the intellectual property rights of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV's (FCA) Jeep brand, barring the sale of the vehicles in question.

Headlines: Take Five: Brextension, Brelection, Bremain
Description: Oct 31 was when Britain was to exit the European Union, with Prime Minister Boris Johnson saying he would rather be "dead in a ditch" than delay Brexit again. But with the UK parliament failing to play along, he's been forced to ask for an extension and the EU will decide on Monday or Tuesday long it will be.

Headlines: Facebook likely to face two more state probes on privacy issues: Bloomberg
Description: Facebook Inc could be subjected to at least two more state probes in the United States on the alleged mishandling of user data, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

Headlines: FCC report found no 'favoritism' on proposed Sinclair deal
Description: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission's inspector general said there was no evidence of impropriety relating to the proposed, and now defunct, merger of Sinclair Broadcast Group  and Tribune Media Co , concluding FCC Chairman Ajit Pai had not shown bias in favor of the deal.

Headlines: Facebook called before Senate panel over digital currency project
Description: Facebook Inc's plans to create a global cryptocurrency will face scrutiny from the U.S. Senate Banking Committee on July 16, the latest sign that policymakers around the globe are casting a wary eye on the project.

Headlines: Samsung to spend more than $14 billion in second phase of China chip plant: Xinhua
Description: South Korean tech giant Samsung Electronics Co Ltd will spend more than $14 billion in the second phase of investment in its memory chip plant in Xian, China, China's official Xinhua news agency reported on Friday citing a Samsung executive.

Headlines: Uber still in the dark on London taxi license renewal, three days before expiry
Description: Uber is waiting to find out whether its taxi license in London, one of its most important markets, will be renewed, just three days before it is due to expire in the latest stage of a long-running battle with the city's transport regulator.

Headlines: Wall Street's sell-off deepens as coronavirus fears intensify
Description: The Dow and the S&P 500 tumbled 3% on Tuesday in their fourth straight day of losses as the coronavirus spread further around the world and investors offloaded risky assets as they struggled to gauge the economic impact.

Headlines: U.S. shale producers eye global pricing as exports surge
Description: Three years after a ban on crude oil exports was lifted, some U.S. shale producers are doing something they have never done before - lock in prices for their barrels that will find a home overseas.

Headlines: Hedge funds increased exposure to growth favorites in first quarter: Goldman
Description: Hedge funds concentrated their portfolios even further into growth stocks including Amazon.com Inc  and Microsoft Corp  in the first quarter of 2020 as the COVID-19 pandemic pummeled U.S. markets, Goldman Sachs analysts said in a report.

Headlines: Take Five: World markets themes for the week ahead
Description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate the thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

Headlines: Occidental finance chief pledges to quickly pare acquisition debt
Description: Occidental Petroleum Corp  expects to quickly reduce the $40 billion in debt it took on with its purchase of Anadarko Petroleum, the company's finance chief said on Monday.

Headlines: U.S.-China trade talks will resume in two weeks: Mnuchin
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Monday that he and U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer would meet with Chinese Vice Premier Liu He for trade talks in two weeks.

Headlines: BNP Paribas CEO rules out big deals when asked about Deutsche Bank
Description: BNP Paribas  chief executive Jean-Laurent Bonnafe effectively ruled out a tie-up with struggling German rival Deutsche Bank  on Thursday, saying the French lender is not considering any large takeovers or mergers.

Headlines: Oil posts first year of losses since 2015
Description: Oil prices ended with full-year losses for the first time since 2015, after a desultory fourth quarter that saw buyers flee the market over growing worries about a supply glut and mixed signals related to renewed U.S. sanctions on Iran.

Headlines: Ethiopia crash may test Boeing's success in defeating U.S. lawsuits: legal experts
Description: The crash of Boeing Co's 737 MAX 8 passenger jet in Ethiopia raises the chances that families of the 157 victims, even non-U.S. residents, will be able to sue in U.S. courts, where payouts are larger than in other countries, some legal experts said.

Headlines: Amazon chief Bezos cashes in $1.8 billion of share pile
Description: Amazon.com Inc  founder Jeff Bezos sold shares worth $1.8 billion in the last three days of July, reducing the value of his stake in the world's third most valuable company to about $110 billion.

Headlines: Pope caps reform of Vatican bank with new statutes
Description: Pope Francis has approved new statutes for the Vatican Bank, making an external audit obligatory and introducing other changes to bolster reforms that have turned around the once scandal-ridden institution.

Headlines: Apple says disappointed with EU antitrust investigations
Description: Apple  on Tuesday accused a few companies of filing groundless complaints and criticised EU antitrust regulators for listening to them and opening two investigations into its Apple Pay and App Store.

Headlines: Kroger to layoff several store employees
Description: Kroger Co  is looking to lay off several store employees holding middle management roles, amidst the supermarket chain's push to improve delivery and in-store technology to attract shoppers.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler says regulators get 'wake-up call' over fuel rules
Description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV  said on Tuesday that U.S. regulators have received a "wake-up call" from automakers over the hurdles they face in trying to meet rising Obama-era fuel-efficiency requirements.

Headlines: Explainer: Germany, France face hurdles in push to rewrite EU antitrust rules
Description: Germany and France want to overhaul EU mergers rules following the European Commission's veto of efforts by Siemens and Alstom to create a European rail champion to compete with larger foreign rivals.

Headlines: Tesla's Musk agrees to new vetting rules for tweets in SEC deal
Description: Tesla Inc Chief Executive Elon Musk has reached a deal with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to settle a dispute over his use of Twitter, agreeing to submit his public statements about the company's finances and other topics to vetting by its legal counsel, according to a court filing on Friday.

Headlines: California developer says virus an act of God, sues Exxon over stalled deal
Description: A California retail developer claims the state's coronavirus lockdown was an act of God that prevented it from completing a $4.2 million property acquisition, asking a court to prevent owner Exxon Mobil Corp from selling to any other buyers.

Headlines: Amazon raises stakes for rivals with one-day delivery goal after profit surge
Description: Amazon.com Inc plans to deliver packages to members of its loyalty club Prime in just one day, instead of two days, part of a spending ramp-up that may curb near-term profits and will up the ante for retail rivals such as Walmart Inc.

Headlines: Wall Street selloff worsens on Mnuchin move, Washington drama
Description: The S&P 500 tumbled to the brink of a bear market on Monday as U.S. stocks extended their steep sell-off in a pre-holiday shortened session, with investors rattled by the U.S. Treasury secretary's convening of a crisis group and by other political developments.

Headlines: Nasdaq says Nordic trader whose deals went sour agrees to sell personal assets
Description: Nasdaq's Nordic commodities exchange has reached agreement on the sale of assets belonging to a private trader who defaulted on his commitments last week, it said on Friday.

Headlines: From cars to quakes: Italy's banks take on insurance
Description: An aging population and struggling state finances could turn into an unlikely boon for Italy's banks, which have turned to a growing market for insurance to brighten their prospects.

Headlines: Thousands of Vodafone UK customers face call connection problems
Description: Thousands of British customers of Vodafone Group Plc , the world's second-biggest mobile operator, faced call connection problems on Tuesday evening, although they were resolved within an hour.

Headlines: Wells Fargo ends forced arbitration for sexual harassment claims
Description: Wells Fargo & Co on Wednesday ended its forced arbitration policy for employee sexual harassment claims, opening the lender to potential lawsuits in the future.

Headlines: Don't see particularly negative aspects in Renault deal: Nissan CEO
Description: Nissan Motor Co doesn't see any particularly negative aspects for it in a possible merger of alliance partner Renault with Fiat Chrysler, the chief executive of the Japanese automaker said on Wednesday.

Headlines: China studying blockchain application for forex - regulator
Description: China is studying the application of blockchain and artificial intelligence in cross-border financing with a focus on risk management, and will further liberalize its capital markets, a senior foreign exchange regulator said on Sunday.

Headlines: American Airlines asks court to block disruptive 'slowdown' by mechanics unions
Description: American Airlines Group Inc has filed a lawsuit against two unions representing its mechanics, asking the court to halt what it called an illegal slowdown that it said on Monday threatened to disrupt U.S. summer travel.

Headlines: China's Great Wall expects mild domestic auto sales growth in second half
Description: Great Wall Motor  expects China's overall auto sales in the second half this year to return to the same level as last year, its president said, as the world's biggest auto market recovers from a coronavirus-driven low.

Headlines: Deere taps tractor-hailing tech in bid to break ground in Africa
Description: It's ride-hailing, farm style. Deere & Co.  is teaming up with the "Uber of tractors" in Africa and betting on a future where farmers summon machines with the touch of a button.

Headlines: U.S. House Speaker Ryan: tariffs not the way to go in China trade dispute
Description: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Paul Ryan said on Wednesday tariffs are not the right tool to use in the trade dispute with China, although Beijing engages in unfair trade practices.

Headlines: Exclusive: Glencore loses exclusive rights to major Libyan oil grades
Description: Trading and mining giant Glencore  has lost its exclusive marketing rights for two of Libya's main crude oil export grades after holding them since late 2015, trading sources with direct knowledge said.

Headlines: China agrees on solution to Tesla customs issue: source
Description: China's customs authorities have accepted electric carmaker Tesla Inc's plan to remedy problems with the clearance of imported cars, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Oil mixed as investors short-cover and Saudi boosts output
Description: Oil was mixed on Friday, with short-covering pushing up U.S. crude futures while Brent slipped on global trade tensions and increased Saudi production.

Headlines: U.S. judge drops some charges against Theranos's Holmes, leaves wire fraud
Description: A federal judge late on Tuesday dismissed some charges against Theranos Inc founder Elizabeth Holmes, but let stand wire fraud charges accusing her and an associate of misleading patients about the abilities of her company's blood tests.

Headlines: Truck makers rev up for rollout of electric big rigs
Description: Tesla Inc  Chief Executive Elon Musk put electric heavy commercial trucks on the map in November 2017 when he unveiled the company's futuristic, battery-powered Semi, booked hundreds of orders and said he would start delivering the vehicles by 2019.

Headlines: Boeing gets first 737 MAX order in months; deliveries halve
Description: Boeing Co  secured the first converted order in months for one of its grounded 737 MAX planes, company data for September showed on Tuesday, as it reported that total deliveries for the first nine months of 2019 had almost halved from a year earlier.

Headlines: Italy's minibonds would either be illegal or useless: finance minister
Description: It would be either illegal or useless for Italy to issue bonds to pay its suppliers as such notes would break European currency rules or add to the country's massive government debt, Italian finance minister Giovanni Tria said on Saturday.

Headlines: Fiat Chrysler/Peugeot deal in spotlight after Exor setbacks
Description: Fiat Chrysler's  decision to scrap its dividend marks another setback for plans by the Agnelli family's Exor  arm to raise cash after a $9 billion sale of its reinsurer unit PartnerRe collapsed this week.

Headlines: Euro zone budget could be conditional on discipline: IMF's Lagarde
Description: IMF Managing Director Christine Lagarde said on Saturday that a proposed joint euro zone budget could be designed with conditions so that it does not become a no-strings-attached transfer of rich countries' cash to poorer members.

Headlines: Americans on COVID-19 jobless benefits spent more than when working, study shows
Description: Americans who received enhanced unemployment benefits due to the coronavirus pandemic spent more than when they were working, a study released on Thursday said, adding to concerns about a steep fall in spending when the emergency benefits expire.

Headlines: Exclusive: Oracle says investigators have asked it for information about Google
Description: Oracle Corp , which has clashed with Alphabet's Google  in business disputes, has received requests for information from congressional and state investigators looking into allegations that Google violated antitrust law.

Headlines: Turkey's Erdogan tells Putin he wants new summit on Syria's Idlib
Description: Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan told Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday he should hold another summit to discuss the situation in Syria's Idlib province where the two countries are trying to create a sustainable demilitarized zone.

Headlines: AirAsia chairman, asked about possible Airbus order, says nothing cemented
Description: Nothing is certain about a reported AirAsia  order for Airbus  A321neo jets until it is announced, and everything is still possible, AirAsia's chairman said when asked about the possible deal.

Headlines: Exclusive: JPMorgan looking to offload Saudi and UAE sovereign fund loans - sources
Description: JPMorgan  is seeking to sell at a discount loans raised by the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, according to two sources and a document, as banks brace for a borrowing spree in the Gulf due to low oil prices.

Headlines: Appaloosa steps up pressure on Allergan to split chairman, CEO roles
Description: Hedge fund Appaloosa LP on Tuesday urged pharmaceutical company Allergan Plc  to split its chairman and chief executive roles, arguing that an independent chair could help CEO Brent Saunders boost the company's sagging share price.

Headlines: China says Canadian stole secrets; Huawei to sue U.S.
Description: China's government and its leading smartphone maker, Huawei Technologies Ltd, stepped up pressure on Monday on the U.S. and Canadian governments in a dispute over trade and telecoms technology that has ensnared Huawei's CFO, who faces U.S. criminal charges.

Headlines: Vietnam carrier Vietjet to suspend flights to China from February 1
Description: Vietnamese carrier Vietjet will suspend all flights to and from China from Feb. 1 over coronavirus concerns, the company said on Friday.

Headlines: Ex-Autonomy CEO Lynch denies new U.S. charges against him
Description: British entrepreneur Mike Lynch vigorously denies new U.S. criminal charges against him, his spokesman said on Saturday ahead of a court case over the sale of his firm Autonomy which will begin in London next week.

Headlines: Elon Musk shoots down U.S. regulator's complaint about his Tesla tweet
Description: SAN FRANCISCO - Tesla Inc  Chief Executive Elon Musk shot back against U.S. securities regulators on Monday, arguing in a filing that his recent tweet about the electric vehicle maker's production volume did not violate his fraud settlement and he cannot be held in contempt.

Headlines: Progress made toward strengthening Argentina program: IMF's Lagarde
Description: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Christine Lagarde said on Tuesday that she and Argentina's Finance Minister made progress toward strengthening the IMF-backed program for Argentina in the face of market volatility.

Headlines: Lexus tops 2019 dependability rankings, Fiat struggles
Description: Toyota Motor's Lexus brand of luxury vehicles was the most dependable name for the eighth consecutive year, while Fiat Chrysler's Fiat brand dropped to the bottom in an annual auto industry reliability survey published Wednesday.

Headlines: High U.S. stock valuations hinge on inflation, interest rates
Description: Investors are banking on tame inflation and interest rates to support U.S. stock prices and help counter any concerns over an anticipated slowdown in corporate earnings growth next year.

Headlines: Swedish FSA says Swedbank situation no threat to financial stability
Description: Swedbank's recent problems with alleged money-laundering has affected trust in the bank, but the situation does not pose a problem to financial stability, the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (FSA) said on Monday.

Headlines: Trump, Britain's Johnson discussed 'telecommunications' after Huawei decision: White House
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump and Britain's Prime Minister Boris Johnson "discussed critical regional and bilateral issues, including telecommunications security" in a conversation on Tuesday, White House spokesman Judd Deere said in a statement.

Headlines: Apple raises production of iPhone 11 models by about 10%: Nikkei
Description: Apple Inc  has asked suppliers to increase production of its iPhone 11 models by up to 8 million units, or about 10%, Nikkei Asian Review reported, hinting that demand for the recently launched versions of its flagship phone was picking up.

Headlines: Sempra Energy CEO 'very optimistic' about talks with Elliott Management
Description: Sempra Energy's  Chief Executive Jeffrey Martin told investors on Monday the company was in a "constructive dialogue" with activist investor Elliott Management, which has been pushing for sweeping changes at the utility.

Headlines: Apple loses $1 trillion status after soft holiday forecast
Description: Shares in Apple Inc  fell 6 percent on Friday, cutting its market value back to less than $1 trillion after it forecast softer-than-expected sales for the holiday quarter and fueled nerves over iPhone sales by saying it would no longer release the figures.

Headlines: Facebook sued for age, gender bias in financial services ads
Description: Facebook Inc was sued on Thursday in a proposed class action accusing it of discriminating against older and female users by withholding advertising for financial services such as bank accounts, insurance, investments and loans.

Headlines: Norwegian Air says its Boeing MAX fleet doesn't have cockpit warning light
Description: Norwegian Air's fleet of 18 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft is not equipped with a cockpit light warning of discrepancies between angle of attack sensors, the company said on Friday.

Headlines: Aston Martin adds FTSE experience to its board ahead of IPO
Description: Aston Martin has lined up experienced FTSE executives to boost its board as the 105-year-old luxury carmaker presses ahead with plans to list on the London Stock Exchange, it said on Monday.

Headlines: Cohen's Point72 to open Warsaw office for some back office teams
Description: Billionaire investor Steven A. Cohen's Point72 Asset Management is opening the $16.2 billion firm's latest satellite location in Warsaw and moving some back office operations to lower-cost Poland.

Headlines: Deutsche, Commerzbank talks private commercial decision: SPD leader
Description: Merger talks between Deutsche Bank and its smaller rival Commerzbank are a private commercial decision, the leader of the German centre-left SPD party, Andrea Nahles, said on Monday.

Headlines: EDF shares jump on hopes re-nationalization will unlock value
Description: EDF shares rose as much as 4.3 percent on Monday on hopes that a partial re-nationalization of the French utility will unlock value and ring-fence EDF's capital-intensive nuclear activities from its renewables and grids.

Headlines: Trump administration unveils Fannie, Freddie overhaul, urges Congress to act
Description: The U.S. Treasury on Thursday said the government should draw up a plan to begin recapitalizing mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, while calling on Congress to pen a comprehensive housing reform that would allow them to be safely freed from government control.

Headlines: Wall Street traders set for best year since aftermath of crisis
Description: Wall Street trading desks may have reached a post-crisis turning point, with revenue on track for the best year since 2011, second-quarter earnings reports from big U.S. banks showed.

Headlines: Kellogg, Mondelez stock up on Pringles, Milka for fear of Brexit
Description: As Brexit looms, Kellogg Co and Mondelez International Inc are taking measures to protect Britons from a potential shortage of Pringles chips, BelVita biscuits and Milka chocolate.

Headlines: Canada ready to cover Kinder Morgan loss, sees outside interest
Description: Canada is prepared to cover some losses Kinder Morgan Canada Ltd might suffer if a proposed oil pipeline expansion is delayed and thinks other investors are ready to step in if need be, Finance Minister Bill Morneau said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Ad infinitum? Mad Men seek new pitch for digital age
Description: Paid to have their finger on the consumer's pulse, the Mad Men of advertising are under mounting pressure from clients to adapt to a fast-changing digital age where simply shifting marketing dollars online from old media no longer cuts it as a strategy.

Headlines: Escalating trade fight weighs on global stocks, boosts Treasuries
Description: Global stock markets sank on Monday as the trade fight between the United States and other top economies escalated, and benchmark Wall Street indexes suffered their worst losses in more than two months while safe-haven investments gained.

Headlines: Exclusive: T. Rowe Price held talks with Guaido team on Venezuela PDVSA 2020 payment
Description: T. Rowe Price has held informal talks with advisors of Venezuelan opposition leader Juan Guaido about financing a $913 million payment on state oil firm PDVSA's 2020 bond, an executive at the U.S. fund manager told Reuters, adding the plan would only work if Washington alters sanctions on Venezuela.

Headlines: Two U.S. coal miners see growth amid sector's gloom
Description: U.S. electric utilities are expected to shut hundreds more of their coal-fired power generators in the coming years, extending a long trend away from coal and toward natural gas that has cast a pall over the mining industry.

Headlines: Qualcomm's licensing forecast, helped by Apple deal, drives share gains
Description: Qualcomm Inc  on Wednesday forecast current-quarter profit above Wall Street expectations, as its all-important licensing segment benefits from a deal with Apple Inc  and the annual holiday-quarter boost it brings.

Headlines: Walmart ups minimum wage in e-commerce warehouses by $2 as orders surge on virus worries
Description: Walmart Inc said on Monday it has temporarily raised entry wages for workers in its e-commerce warehouses by $2, following similar moves by rivals, as it attempts to manage a shopping surge brought about by the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Risk of U.S. 'profit recession' eases as results beat forecasts
Description: The initial earnings results of this reporting period are beating expectations by a wide margin, suggesting to some investors that the S&P 500 may be able to avoid a so-called "profit recession" this year because predicted economic bad news has failed to materialize.

Headlines: Facebook plans content oversight board, tightens paid ad rules
Description: Facebook Inc on Monday laid out plans for an independent content oversight board with the power to overturn company decisions on user posts, aimed at addressing concerns over misinformation and abusive behavior on the platform.

Headlines: Big U.S. banks halt stock buybacks, citing customer needs during coronavirus
Description: The United States' biggest banks will stop buying back their own shares, and will instead use that capital to lend to individuals and businesses affected by the coronavirus, an industry trade group said on Sunday.

Headlines: Korean Air to buy 20 Boeing 787s, lease 10 more
Description: (This June 19 story corrects to fix types of aircraft being purchased and leased in paragraph 2)

Headlines: Boeing says has no new guidance for 737 MAX 8 operators
Description: Boeing said on Monday the investigation into the Ethiopian Airlines crash is in its early stages and there is no need to issue new guidance to operators of its 737 MAX 8 aircraft based on the information it has so far.

Headlines: SoftBank says Vision Fund 2 could start investing soon, bags big gains on first
Description: SoftBank Group Corp's  second Vision Fund could start investing as soon as next month, founder and Chief Executive Masayoshi Son said, as the technology conglomerate reported a leap in profits at its first $100 billion fund.

Headlines: Nintendo's Mario takes driving seat in race for mobile hit
Description: Nintendo Co Ltd  is set to bring one of its most successful franchises to mobile for the first time on Wednesday with the global launch of Mario Kart Tour, in a test of the gaming firm's strategy to drive growth beyond consoles.

Headlines: China to buy additional $32 billion in U.S. farm goods over two years, sign deal in January: USTR
Description: China has agreed to buy $32 billion of additional U.S. farm products over two years as part of a phase one trade pact, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer told reporters on Friday, adding the deal would be signed the first week of January.

Headlines: Carmaker PSA cuts back on transfer of Polish workers to French plant
Description: France's PSA , the maker of Peugeot cars, on Monday said it would only transfer a small group of Polish workers to help out in a French plant where production is being increased, following a backlash over the knock-on effect for local jobs.

Headlines: Bitcoin goes through third 'halving', falls vs U.S. dollar
Description: Bitcoin slid on Monday in volatile trading, after it went through a technical adjustment that reduced the rate at which new coins are created, but the outlook remained upbeat as the increase in supply slows down.

Headlines: Japan watchdog to recommend $24 million fine for Nissan over Ghosn pay: source
Description: Japan's markets watchdog will likely recommend that the financial regulator fine Nissan Motor Co up to 4 billion yen ($37 million) over the alleged underreporting of former Chairman Carlos Ghosn's compensation, a source said.

Headlines: Better battery packaging on planes overlooks other safety concerns: airlines
Description: New global packaging standards expected in late 2018 will allow lithium-ion batteries back into passenger plane cargo holds, pending design and regulatory approval, but some airlines say the new rule overlooks other safety concerns.

Headlines: Exclusive: Qatar Petroleum - coronavirus turmoil will not stop LNG expansion abroad
Description: Qatar Petroleum (QP) is pressing ahead with foreign as well as domestic expansion despite the global market turmoil caused by the coronavirus pandemic, its chief executive told Reuters on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. isolated at G7 meeting as tariffs prompt retaliation
Description: The United States' closest allies attacked the Trump administration on Friday for imposing tariffs on steel and aluminum imports and mounted challenges with the world's top trade body, fouling the mood at a G7 finance leaders meeting.

Headlines: Facebook moves to rate users on trustworthiness: report
Description: Facebook Inc  has started scoring its users based on their trustworthiness in an attempt to fight misinformation, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday, citing a company executive.

Headlines: UK accounting watchdog examining EY audit of Thomas Cook
Description: Britain's Financial Reporting Council has started an investigation into accountant EY's audit of Thomas Cook, the travel company that collapsed last month leaving tens of thousands of holiday-makers stranded abroad.

Headlines: Ford hires new China chief to tackle daunting turnaround task
Description: Ford Motor Co  has hired a new chief for its troubled China operations, ending a nine-month search after the previous head suddenly quit and tasking him with fixing a deep sales slump in the world's biggest car market.

Headlines: Google defeats lawsuit claiming YouTube censors conservatives
Description: Google has won the dismissal of a lawsuit in California accusing YouTube of censoring conservative content.

Headlines: General Electric says blade problem affects more gas turbines
Description: General Electric Co  said on Friday that turbine blade oxidation which forced Exelon Corp  to idle four electric power units in Texas also affects another model, widening the impact of the latest problem to hit GE's ailing power unit.

Headlines: Madame Tussauds owner Merlin to be bought by Lego family and Blackstone
Description: Madame Tussauds owner Merlin Entertainments  is to be acquired by the investment vehicle of Lego's founding family and private equity firm Blackstone Group LP  in a deal valuing the company and its debt at nearly 6 billion pounds ($7.6 billion).

Headlines: U.S. sets China trade deal terms, sources say, but Beijing mum
Description: Washington has set its terms for a trade deal with China,  offering to suspend some tariffs on Chinese goods and cut others in exchange for Beijing's buying more American farm goods, U.S. sources said on Thursday.

Headlines: Barclays gets capital boost ahead of potential coronavirus loan losses
Description: Barclays  told investors on Monday that recent regulatory changes had boosted its core capital, giving the British bank a bigger buffer to absorb any further loan losses during the coronavirus crisis.

Headlines: Pfizer warns of hit to financial results on continued coronavirus outbreak
Description: Pfizer Inc  on Thursday warned that the continued spread of the coronavirus globally could have an adverse impact on its business and financial results.

Headlines: Amazon earnings skyrocket on cloud computing, advertising
Description: Amazon.com Inc  forecast strong fall sales and posted a profit that was double Wall Street targets on Thursday thanks to the retailer's younger, higher-earning businesses, including cloud computing and advertising.

Headlines: Japan, U.S. ministers meet for trade talks as hopes for early deal fade
Description: Japan and the United States will seek to narrow gaps on trade when their top negotiators meet this week, but hopes for a deal in September are fading as both sides fail to make concessions on agriculture and automobiles, sources say.

Headlines: Factbox: What happens at the Fed's rate-setting meetings?
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve concluded its latest two-day policy meeting on Wednesday to set a key U.S. interest rate that impacts investors, consumers, and companies around the world.

Headlines: Exclusive: RBS lawyers ask ex-staffer to destroy documents, DOJ informed
Description: Lawyers for Royal Bank of Scotland  asked an ex-employee to destroy confidential documents, according to a letter seen by Reuters, in a move which the former staffer's lawyer said put him at risk of legal action by the U.S. government.

Headlines: Ryanair passengers down by 99.6% in April, Wizz Air down by 97.6%
Description: Europe's biggest budget airline Ryanair  posted a 99.6% fall in passenger numbers in April, while smaller low cost carrier Wizz Air  said numbers plunged 97.6%, as the novel coronavirus halted most flying across Europe.

Headlines: Toyota snub dents Saudi Arabia's manufacturing drive
Description: Saudi Arabia began courting Toyota two years ago to build a large car plant as part of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's grand plan to wean the kingdom off oil revenues and create jobs for young Saudis.

Headlines: Tesla up 20% after Panasonic posts first quarterly profit at battery business
Description: Tesla Inc's stock surged 20% on Monday in its largest one-day gain since 2013, fueled by a quarterly profit at Panasonic's battery business with the U.S. car maker and an investor report predicting its shares would rise more than ten-fold by 2024.

Headlines: Australian regulator says 'extensive' investigation behind looming charges against ANZ, Deutsche
Description: Australia's competition regulator said the criminal cartel charges it expects to lay against Deutsche Bank  and Australia and New Zealand Banking Group  over a 2015 ANZ share issue follow an "extensive investigation".

Headlines: FAA should mandate safety management systems for Boeing, others: panel
Description: An expert committee on Thursday recommended the Federal Aviation Administration require Boeing Co  and other aircraft manufacturers to adopt new safety management tools in the wake of two fatal Boeing 737 MAX crashes that killed 346 people.

Headlines: George Soros' bet on Tesla could see other investors follow suit
Description: If Tesla Inc  Chief Executive Elon Musk needs to raise even more money, there may be a way.

Headlines: Wingardium Leviosa! Harry Potter magic helps Lego lift sales
Description: Harry Potter and Star Wars building sets helped Lego return to growth in 2018, along with strong sales in China, where the privately-owned Danish toymaker plans to open new stores.

Headlines: South Korea picks Boeing P-8 for $1.7 billion maritime patrol aircraft contract
Description: South Korea's military has picked Boeing Co  to supply the country's maritime patrol aircraft in a contract worth around 1.9 trillion won ($1.71 billion), a senior company executive said on Monday.

Headlines: Harley-Davidson's profit beats estimates, shares rally
Description: Harley-Davidson Inc's  shares rallied on Tuesday after the motorcycle maker forecast a lower-than-expected hit to profit margins from U.S. President Donald Trump's trade tariffs and its quarterly earnings topped Wall Street estimates.

Headlines: JP Morgan Australia chairman resigns from bourse directorship over cartel case
Description: JP Morgan's chairman of Australian operations has resigned from his directorships at the country's bourse and sovereign wealth fund citing complications arising from a criminal prosecution over a stock issue the investment bank was joint-lead on.

Headlines: U.S. takes aim at judges pay in new attack on WTO system
Description: Judges at the World Trade Organization can earn more than 300,000 Swiss francs tax-free for what is a part-time job, the United States said on Friday, in a fresh onslaught on its beleaguered arbitration system.

Headlines: Top Sainsbury's shareholder QIA backs Asda takeover talks: source
Description: Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), the biggest shareholder in J Sainsbury Plc, is supportive of merger talks between the British supermarket chain and rival Walmart Inc's Asda, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Headlines: Rolls-Royce, preparing to cut thousands of jobs, says engine problem has spread
Description: Britain's Rolls-Royce  said a costly compressor problem that had grounded Boeing planes had now been found in a different type of engine, compounding pressures on a group that is due to cut more than 4,000 jobs this week.

Headlines: Japan Airlines looks to deepen partnership with Malaysia Airlines
Description: Japan Airlines Co Ltd (JAL) may expand a joint venture with Malaysia Airlines to cover U.S. flights and other Asian routes in the future, the Japanese carrier's president said.

Headlines: U.S. markets regulators reach deal on Dodd-Frank swaps capital rules
Description: U.S. markets regulators on Friday unveiled an agreement on how much capital and margin firms must hold when trading swaps based on securities, finalizing a key piece of the 2010 Dodd-Frank law introduced following the 2007-09 financial crisis.

Headlines: Escalating fight, Trump sues Deutsche Bank, Capital One over Democratic subpoenas
Description: President Donald Trump, his three oldest children and the Trump Organization have sued Deutsche Bank AG and Capital One Financial Corp to try to block them from responding to U.S. congressional subpoenas issued by Democrats seeking financial records.

Headlines: JP Morgan's Dimon says U.S. economy still looks 'pretty good'
Description: JPMorgan Chase  Chief Executive Jamie Dimon said on Wednesday the U.S. economy still looked "pretty good" and that there was no law that says growth cannot continue.

Headlines: Emissions rules and electric shift to spur car engines M&A
Description: A growing understanding in the car industry of the value of combustion engine technology able to meet new anti-pollution requirements is likely to fuel a wave of consolidation in the next two years, industry executives and bankers say.

Headlines: Volkswagen sounds out buyers for MAN Energy Solutions -sources
Description: Volkswagen has approached several companies to gauge their appetite for buying MAN Energy Solutions, which makes large diesel engines for ships and power generators, people close to the matter said.

Headlines: U.S. funds remain cautious faced with trade war threat: Reuters poll
Description: U.S. fund managers in June replicated defensive recommendations from the previous month with slightly more cash, a Reuters poll showed, underscoring worries that a U.S. trade conflict with China and some of its own allies will hurt global growth.

Headlines: Architect of Trump tax cut may run $500 billion coronavirus loan program
Description: U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Justin Muzinich, an architect of the sweeping 2017 Republican tax cut, is under consideration to oversee a newly created $500 billion coronavirus rescue loan program for large companies, cities and states, two sources familiar with the agency's plans said.

Headlines: United Airlines first-quarter profit rises, holds 2019 target
Description: United Airlines on Tuesday reported a better-than-expected jump in first-quarter profit as it sold more tickets and cut costs, standing by its 2019 profit target even as its Boeing Co 737 MAX jets remain grounded.

Headlines: Union Pacific cost cuts sheltered profit amid freight slowdown
Description: Union Pacific Corp  on Thursday reported a quarterly profit that beat Wall Street estimates, as the U.S. railroad operator cut costs and raised rates to overcome disruptions from record floods in the Midwest and ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions.

Headlines: Britain concerned by U.S.-China trade tensions: UK PM's spokeswoman
Description: Britain is concerned by the escalating tariff tensions between the United States and China and believes no one benefits from a trade war, a spokeswoman for Prime Minister Theresa May said on Friday.

Headlines: Macron says concerned about conditions of Ghosn's detention in Japan
Description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Sunday he has expressed concern to Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe over the prison conditions faced by former Renault boss Carlos Ghosn.

Headlines: U.S.-China trade hopes lift stocks; oil hits three-month high
Description: Stocks rose in major markets across the world on Friday on bets of progress in trade talks between China and the United States, while crude futures hit their highest level in more than three months supported by ongoing supply cuts.

Headlines: Fed balance sheet tops $5 trillion for first time as it enters coronavirus war mode
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve's balance sheet soared past $5 trillion in assets for the first time this week as it scooped up bonds and extended loans to banks, mutual funds and other central banks in its unprecedented effort to backstop the economy in the face of the global coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: U.S., European regulators to meet with Boeing this week on 737 MAX software audit
Description: U.S. and European aviation safety regulators will meet with Boeing this week in an effort to complete a 737 MAX software documentation audit - a key step toward the grounded plane's eventual return to service.

Headlines: Intel creates chip to control quantum computers
Description: Quantum computers aim to carry out tasks in just a few minutes that would take today's best conventional computers thousands of years. But in nearly every photograph of the devices, there's a tangle of wires in the background connected to equipment that controls the quantum computer.

Headlines: Dow cuts 2019 spending forecast on U.S-China trade tensions
Description: Dow Inc  forecast current-quarter revenue below analysts' expectations on Thursday and cut 2019 spending as chemical companies grapple with U.S.-China trade dispute and an oversupply of chemicals used to make plastics.

Headlines: Saudi Arabia still moving ahead with three major development projects
Description: Saudi Arabia is still moving ahead with three major development projects, NEOM, the Red Sea tourism project, and an entertainment development that will include a Six Flags theme park.

Headlines: Exclusive: Alibaba-backed startup AutoX applies for driver-less test permit in California
Description: Chinese startup AutoX, backed by e-commerce giant Alibaba, has applied to test self-driving vehicles without an in-car backup driver in California, the first challenger to Alphabet Inc's autonomous driving venture Waymo to say it has done so.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp CEO's last roll of the dice: sell the family silver
Description: Thyssenkrupp  CEO Guido Kerkhoff has little choice but to sell the group's prized elevator division lock, stock and barrel so he can save the conglomerate's remaining businesses, four sources close to the German company said.

Headlines: DHL struggles to cope as online parcel volumes surge
Description: Delivery business DHL  is struggling to cope with a flood of parcels from online purchases due to the coronavirus crisis, forcing it to cut back extra collections from retailers in Germany, parent company Deutsche Post said on Thursday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Standard Chartered sells principal finance business to Actis and ICG
Description: Standard Chartered  is in talks to sell its private equity business to Intermediate Capital Group  (ICG), a source with direct knowledge of the deal said on Monday, as part of a broader disposal of its 'principal finance' investment business.

Headlines: Justice Department probes whether social media is 'stifling' speech
Description: The U.S. Department of Justice and state attorneys general will meet this month to discuss concerns that social media platforms are "intentionally stifling the free exchange of ideas," the department said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Papa John's picks hedge fund Starboard over founder for investment
Description: By Svea Herbst-Bayliss, Uday Sampath Kumar and Harry Brumpton

Headlines: Triumvirate to run strike-hit Air France-KLM for now after pay row
Description: Air France-KLM  installed a triumvirate of executives led by its finance chief to run the strike-hit airline while it searches for a new CEO, following a standoff over staff pay.

Headlines: Rusal says board backs change of domicile to Russia
Description: Russia's sanctions-hit aluminum giant Rusal  said on Friday its board had discussed and approved a change of domicile from Britain's Jersey to Russia in order to take advantage of new special tax regulations.

Headlines: NY Fed markets head says 'time is of the essence' in establishing new lending facilities
Description: The Federal Reserve responded rapidly to stem losses from a "synchronized global sell-off" to help markets function as investors fled to safety on worries about the coronavirus outbreak, a senior official at the New York Fed said on Friday.

Headlines: Consumer groups, unions urge caution on $63 billion AbbVie deal for Allergan
Description: About a dozen advocacy groups and unions, including Public Citizen and the American Federation of Teachers, wrote the Federal Trade Commission on Thursday urging it to consider blocking drugmaker AbbVie Inc's  planned $63 billion purchase of Botox maker Allergan Plc .

Headlines: Consultation prize: U.S.-China trade war fires bonanza for advisory firms
Description: As U.S. and Chinese firms rush for outside expertise on how to handle fallout from the escalating trade war between the two nations, consultants on everything from management to logistics say they have seen soaring demand for their services.

Headlines: Walmart acquires online lingerie retailer Bare Necessities
Description: Walmart Inc  said on Friday it has acquired online lingerie retailer Bare Necessities for an undisclosed amount, its second apparel-focused acquisition in less than two weeks as it seeks deeper inroads into the online fashion space.

Headlines: Italy arrests Siemens, Alstom executives over Milan subway deals
Description: Italian tax police arrested 13 people, including executives of the Italian units of Germany's Siemens  and France's Alstom , in an investigation into alleged bribery relating to Milan subway contracts, prosecutors said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Airbus in talks to unjam some HNA, Emirates deliveries: sources
Description: Airbus faces new headaches delivering A330s to airlines tied to China's cash-strapped HNA Group and is in separate talks with Emirates over the timing of undelivered A380 superjumbos.

Headlines: Rolls-Royce, Airbus to collaborate on new UltraFan engine
Description: Rolls-Royce  and Airbus  have signed a deal to  collaborate on development of the UltraFan, a new engine that is intended to 25 percent more fuel efficient than the earliest version of the Trent engine, the British company said on Wednesday.

Headlines: U.S. sets record for new COVID cases third day in a row at over 69,000
Description: New cases of COVID-19 rose by over 69,000 across the United States on Friday, according to a Reuters tally, setting a record for the third consecutive day as Walt Disney Co stuck to its plans to reopen its flagship theme park in hard-hit Florida.

Headlines: Automakers boost Takata air bag recall completion rates
Description: Automakers in the United States repaired more than 7.2 million defective Takata air bag inflators in 2018, as companies have ramped up efforts to track down parts in need of replacement, a report from an independent monitor released on Friday said.

Headlines: Avenatti says 'nervous' about prison time but proclaims innocence
Description: Michael Avenatti on Tuesday again proclaimed his innocence on charges he tried to extort millions of dollars from Nike Inc, but in an interview with CBS, admitted he was concerned about doing prison time.

Headlines: Berlin welcomes carmakers' trade-in offers
Description: The government welcomes German automakers' moves towards making concrete offers of discount trade-ins to owners of older, dirtier diesel vehicles, adding that these latest moves had been precisely what Chancellor Angela Merkel had been expecting.

Headlines: Aldi takes on U.S. rivals with scores of new products
Description: German-owned discount supermarket Aldi Inc is rolling out scores of new products in the United States, it said on Thursday, in an aggressive push to expand in the country even as rivals are struggling in a drawn-out price war.

Headlines: Irish regulator nears end of first privacy probe, ruling to take months
Description: Ireland's data privacy regulator is close to concluding its first probe into a multinational company under the EU's new privacy laws, likely to involve Facebook's WhatsApp subsidiary, although a formal decision could take months.

Headlines: Beer sales growth still seen elusive in Russia as World Cup looms
Description: The prospect of thousands of thirsty soccer fans flocking to Russia for this summer's World Cup should offer a big boost for the country's beer market, yet brewers see little reason to be optimistic.

Headlines: Pompeo: 'No mixed messages' from U.S. on Huawei
Description: U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said on Tuesday the United States was not sending "mixed messages" on Huawei Technologies and he does not believe a U.S. blacklist of the Chinese telecommunications giant will block a trade deal with Beijing.

Headlines: Adidas extends sponsorship of Real Madrid until 2028
Description: Adidas will extend its sponsorship of Spanish soccer side Real Madrid until 2028, the German sportswear firm said on Wednesday, as it battles fierce competition in Europe from Nike and a resurgent Puma.

Headlines: Aramco more resilient to oil slump than listed rivals: accounts
Description: Saudi Aramco is more resilient to oil price slumps than its biggest listed rivals, its 2016 accounts indicate, giving a rare insight into the state energy giant's finances ahead of a proposed flotation.

Headlines: Exclusive: Sinopec USA turns copper buyer to supply China operations - sources
Description: The U.S. unit of China's oil major Sinopec Corp  is procuring copper to send to its equipment suppliers in China, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters, a rare move by a Chinese oil company.

Headlines: BA, Ryanair, easyJet protest over 'wholly unjustified' UK quarantine plan
Description: Three airlines have written to the British government in protest at its "wholly unjustified and disproportionate" quarantine rules for most international arrivals from Monday, a copy of the letter seen by Reuters showed.

Headlines: Aerion's supersonic business jet to meet U.S. noise standards
Description: Aerion Supersonic, the developer of a $120 million supersonic business jet, said on Monday it would be able to take off and land without regulatory changes in the United States, a potential boost to efforts to bring back faster air travel.

Headlines: Exclusive: CVS to cover migraine drugs from Teva, Lilly; excludes Amgen
Description: CVS Health Corp, a top U.S. manager of pharmacy benefits, has added new migraine drugs from Teva Pharmaceutical Industries and Eli Lilly and Co to its list of covered drugs, excluding a rival treatment from Amgen Inc, a CVS spokeswoman told Reuters on Friday.

Headlines: Owning Tesla shares about the riskiest it has ever been: options data
Description: Owning electric carmaker Tesla Inc's shares is close to the riskiest it has ever been, data by options database and analytics firm OptionMetrics showed on Wednesday.

Headlines: China says holding 'in-depth' talks with U.S. on interim trade deal
Description: China and the United States are holding "in-depth" discussions on a first phase trade agreement, and cancelling tariffs is an important condition to reaching a deal, the Chinese commerce ministry said on Thursday.

Headlines: Brexit seen threatening UK links in EU supply chain
Description: Mandy Ridyard knew Brexit was going to be a challenge for her aviation components firm, but it was still a shock when she heard a French company bluntly ruling out British suppliers from an international bid for a contract in China.

Headlines: Sainsbury's Coupe says exit not due to failure of Asda deal
Description: The boss of British supermarket group Sainsbury's , Mike Coupe, said he was not stepping down in May because of his failure to buy rival Asda last year.
