Description: The Federal Reserve may wind down its gradual asset-shedding operation sooner than thought, leaving the U.S. central bank with a bigger balance sheet than earlier anticipated, Fed Chairman Jerome Powell said Wednesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: China central bank sees benchmark rate cut as last resort, may use other tools - sources
Description: China's central bank is not yet ready to cut benchmark interest rates to spur the slowing economy, despite cooling inflation and a stronger yuan, which have fanned market expectations of such a move, policy sources told Reuters.

Headlines: UK wants a big U.S. trade deal but health and food standards not up for grabs
Description: Britain said on Monday it will seek to achieve huge gains by removing barriers to trade with the United States in talks for a deal this year but its health service would not be on the table in talks.

Headlines: White House handling of U.S.-Japan trade deal angers Democrats
Description: House Democrats on Wednesday blasted the Trump administration for not consulting sufficiently with Congress while negotiating a mini trade deal with Japan, failing to provide details about it and refusing to testify at a congressional hearing.

Headlines: Roche, joining rivals, donates hemophilia drug to boost access
Description: Switzerland's Roche will donate its new hemophilia A drug Hemlibra to a World Hemophilia Federation program, it said on Wednesday, joining rivals who also back the effort to help patients in developing countries who face treatment hurdles.

Headlines: U.S., Mexico reach NAFTA deal, turn up pressure on Canada
Description: The United States and Mexico agreed on Monday to overhaul the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), putting pressure on Canada to agree to new terms on auto trade and dispute settlement rules to remain part of the three-nation pact.

Headlines: Goldman Sachs' stock-based pay ratio still much higher than rivals'
Description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc pays employees a much bigger portion in stock than Wall Street rivals, a trend that has come into sharper focus as the bank overhauls its business strategy.

Headlines: Exclusive: HNA-linked Hong Kong Airlines seeks $255 million from backers to keep license
Description: Hong Kong Airlines shareholders have demanded to see 2018 accounts before considering providing at least HK$2 billion ($255 million) needed to ensure the carrier - part owned by the indebted HNA Group - keeps its license, two sources said.

Headlines: Facebook and Twitter must comply with EU consumer rules or face sanctions
Description: Facebook  and Twitter  face sanctions unless they comply with European consumer rules by the end of the year, the EU said as its regulators continue to their crackdown on U.S. social media giants over privacy concerns.

Headlines: Turkish Airlines may delay delivery of Airbus, Boeing planes: report
Description: Turkish Airlines , which halted nearly all of its passenger flights as a result of the coronavirus crisis, may delay the delivery of some Boeing  and Airbus  planes, its chairman was quoted as saying on Wednesday.

Headlines: Metro will correct Russia situation soon: CEO
Description: The chief executive of Metro  is hopeful that the German retailer will turn around its struggling Russian business soon, he said on Monday.

Headlines: Coronavirus patients flood hospitals in Swiss canton next to Italy
Description: The southern Swiss canton of Ticino on the border with Italy is being swamped with coronavirus patients and authorities are battling to find enough intensive care beds, a top public health official said on Thursday.

Headlines: Ghosn lawyer says he's optimistic former Nissan head could soon win bail
Description: The lawyer for former Nissan Motor Co Ltd Chairman Carlos Ghosn on Monday said he was optimistic the ousted executive could win bail in the near future, after being held in custody at a detention center in Japan for over three months.

Headlines: Wall St. slips; banks fall with prospect of rate cut, energy drops
Description: Wall Street ended down slightly on Wednesday, with bank stocks declining as prospects of a U.S. interest rate cut rose and energy shares tumbling along with oil prices.

Headlines: Famed Cullinan mine banks on big diamonds to drive down debt
Description: The owner of one of the world's most famous diamond mines could be about a decade away from clearing its multi-million-dollar debts, in a sign of the struggles facing an industry assailed by synthetic rivals and uncertain demand.

Headlines: Gucci owner Kering halts spending in China on virus fears
Description: Gucci-owner Kering has temporarily shut half of its stores in China, and shelved new openings and advertising campaigns there,  as the coronavirus outbreak throws luxury brands into turmoil.

Headlines: China to parade aviation prowess at November expo, but C919 jet a no-show
Description: China will show off its growing military aviation strength at its biggest airshow in November, with fighter jet flypasts and its largest display of weaponry ever, an air force spokesman said on Thursday.

Headlines: Negative U.S. rate bets persist, but seen unlikely to happen
Description: Negative U.S. interest rates could be the norm next year and all through to 2023 if fed funds futures are any indication. Or it could just be traders hedging their bets.

Headlines: U.S. DOJ says pursuing investigations related to Malaysia's 1MDB
Description: The U.S Department of Justice said on Tuesday it would continue to pursue investigations into 1 Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and looked forward to working with Malaysian law enforcement authorities, which have reopened a probe into the fund following a change of government this month.

Headlines: Oil, copper slip as U.S.-China trade fight escalates
Description: Oil and copper prices edged lower on Thursday as the U.S.-China trade dispute escalated while global equity markets fell as gains in U.S. technology shares failed to offset declines in commodity-related and trade-sensitive stocks.

Headlines: U.S. appeals court asks why Facebook encryption order should stay sealed
Description: Federal appeals court judges asked prosecutors on Tuesday why a lower court could seal a ruling that absolved Facebook from having to wiretap a criminal suspect using one of the company’s encrypted services.

Headlines: Trump says U.S., China have reached substantial phase-1 trade deal
Description: President Donald Trump said on Friday the United States and China had come to a substantial phase-1 trade deal, reaching agreement on intellectual property, financial services and big agricultural purchases.

Headlines: Factbox: What happens if the U.S. terminates NAFTA
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he would soon give formal notice to the U.S. Congress to terminate the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), giving lawmakers six months to approve a new trade deal between the United States, Mexico and Canada to replace it.

Headlines: Drillers give tepid response to record U.S. offshore lease sale
Description: Oil and gas drillers bid on only a tiny fraction of Gulf of Mexico acreage offered on Wednesday in the largest lease sale in American history, a setback to the Trump administration's efforts to rapidly pump up investment in the region.

Headlines: France's Total sees natural gas demand far outpacing oil
Description: French oil and gas company Total SA expects the global natural gas market to grow far faster than that for crude oil over the next two decades thanks to booming demand for the cleaner-burning fuel in Asia, an outlook that underpinned Total's recent big investments in the space, Chief Executive Patrick Pouyanne said on Monday.

Headlines: U.S. manufacturing activity plunges to 11-year low as orders sink
Description: U.S. manufacturing activity plunged to an 11-year low in April as the novel coronavirus wreaked havoc on supply chains, suggesting the economy was sinking deeper into recession.

Headlines: Big banks score win as U.S. regulator proposes easing post-crisis derivatives rules
Description: A U.S. banking regulator on Tuesday proposed easing a rule requiring banks to set aside cash to safeguard derivatives trades between affiliates, marking one of the biggest wins for Wall Street lenders under the business-friendly Trump administration.

Headlines: Huawei's HiSilicon says it has long been preparing for U.S. ban scenario
Description: Huawei Technologies' chip arm HiSilicon said on Friday it has long been prepared for the "extreme scenario" that it could be banned from purchasing U.S. chips and technology, and is able to ensure steady supply of most products.

Headlines: Powered by SUVs, Hyundai turns in best quarter since early 2017
Description: Hyundai Motor Co  turned in its best quarterly operating profit in over two years and said it was on track for higher profit margins in 2020, powered by more sales of sport-utility vehicles (SUVs) such as the Palisade and Kona.

Headlines: Alibaba founder defends overtime work culture as 'huge blessing'
Description: Alibaba Group founder and billionaire Jack Ma has defended the grueling overtime work culture at many of China's tech companies, calling it a "huge blessing" for young workers.

Headlines: Over 40 countries object at WTO to U.S. car tariff plan
Description: Major U.S. trading partners including the European Union, China and Japan voiced deep concern at the World Trade Organization (WTO) on Tuesday about possible U.S. measures imposing additional duties on imported autos and parts.

Headlines: Exclusive: Tesla targets November 2019 for start of Model Y production - sources
Description: Tesla Inc  is targeting November 2019 as the start of production for its Model Y sport utility vehicle, with production in China to begin two years later, two sources told Reuters this week, shedding some light on the electric vehicle maker's next project that could tax its resources and capacity.

Headlines: VW's Skoda targets Indian revival with tougher safety, emission rules
Description: Skoda is hoping government moves to drag regulations for cars sold in India up to developed market standards will help turn around its fortunes in a market where it has stalled.

Headlines: Coronavirus widens the cracks in Egypt's cement industry
Description: The coronavirus is putting Egypt's private cement industry under even more pressure.

Headlines: Deutsche Bank in partnership talks with SoftBank-backed OakNorth: source
Description: Deutsche Bank  is in talks with SoftBank-backed  British fintech firm OakNorth to use the latter's credit analysis and monitoring platform, a source with knowledge of the discussions told Reuters.

Headlines: Amazon opens pop-up store on China's Pinduoduo until year-end
Description: Amazon.com Inc on Monday said it will open a pop-up store on Chinese e-commerce platform Pinduoduo Inc that will run until the end of December and carry a selection of about 1,000 products from overseas.

Headlines: Exclusive: Saudi's Falih says no OPEC+ output policy change until June
Description: Saudi oil minister Khalid al-Falih said on Sunday it would be too early to change OPEC+ output policy at the group's meeting in April and that China and the U.S. would lead healthy global demand for oil this year.

Headlines: China's factory activity expands, but job losses quicken amid weak exports: Caixin PMI
Description: China's factory activity grew at a faster clip in June after the government lifted coronavirus lockdown measures and ramped up support steps, but the health crisis continues to pressure exports and jobs, a private business survey showed on Wednesday.

Headlines: Conoco waiting for Venezuela to pay $2 billion settlement: CEO
Description: U.S. oil producer ConocoPhillips  is still awaiting payment from Venezuela on a $2 billion arbitration settlement reached last month with the country's state-run PDVSA, Chief Executive Ryan Lance said on Wednesday.

Headlines: What do the Fed's latest moves mean for U.S. consumers?
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve unleashed new emergency measures on Sunday night to limit the economic harm from the coronavirus, including making it easier for banks to get money and slashing its benchmark borrowing rate to near zero.

Headlines: Activists in dinghy urge Credit Suisse off climate 'collision course'
Description: Climate activists clad in Titanic-era costumes gathered in a rubber dinghy outside Credit Suisse's headquarters on Thursday, to urge incoming chief executive Thomas Gottstein to steer the bank off a climate "collision course".

Headlines: Exclusive: GE seeking to shed troubled insurance business - sources
Description: General Electric Co  is working with investment bankers to find ways to shed its insurance business, which has caused it to book hefty charges while sparking shareholder lawsuits and an investigation by U.S. regulators, people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Exclusive: Top lithium miner seeks to monitor water scarcity in parched Chile salt flat
Description: With residents and courts ringing the alarm about depleted water supplies in Chile's Atacama salt flat, the world's top lithium miner Albemarle  quietly filed a proposal in December for a network to monitor flows beneath the parched desert floor.

Headlines: CNH Industrial's Iveco unveils first electric truck in partnership with Nikola
Description: CNH Industrial's truck unit Iveco on Tuesday unveiled its first electric vehicle, the Nikola Tre, built in partnership with U.S. startup Nikola Motor Co..

Headlines: In search of higher margins, Canada Goose to make more of its own luxury coats
Description: Luxury coat maker Canada Goose plans to bring more manufacturing in-house in a bid to boost margins and help it live up to lofty investor expectations as the most expensive stock among major luxury brands.

Headlines: U.S.-China trade talks 'made progress' but 'significant work remains': White House
Description: The White House said on Friday after three days of trade talks with Chinese officials in Washington that the negotiations "made progress on numerous key issues" but "significant work remains."

Headlines: China iron ore imports fall to 18-month low in April as Brazil shipments slide
Description: China's iron ore imports in April fell to the lowest level in 18 months as poor weather in Brazil, the country's second-biggest supplier, disrupted shipments and some production by miner Vale SA was halted after a mine accident.

Headlines: Kill quarterly reporting? Some investors ring alarm bells
Description: Less reporting by U.S. corporations could put shareholders in the dark, allow companies to drift off course and even make U.S. stocks less attractive and create less public company investment, some investors and analysts argue.

Headlines: Elliott adds voice to calls for Whitbread break-up
Description: Hedge fund Elliott Advisors has become the second activist investor to call for Whitbread  to split its hotel and coffee shop businesses after emerging as the largest shareholder in the British company.

Headlines: Last man standing: lonely Fed tightening spurs dollar surge
Description: As speculation about interest rate rises and policy 'normalization' in the euro zone, Japan, Britain and China falls away rapidly, the U.S. Federal Reserve's now lonely monetary tightening has suddenly supercharged the dollar.

Headlines: Ghosn lawyer says news conference canceled after his daughters raised concerns
Description: Former Nissan Chairman Carlos Ghosn canceled what would have been his first news conference since he was arrested last year after his daughters expressed concern about the potential consequences, his lawyer said on Friday.

Headlines: Facebook says all directors elected, shareholder proposals rejected
Description: All eight of Facebook Inc's  director nominees were elected at its annual meeting on Thursday, and all six shareholder proposals urging reforms, including to its voting structure and content oversight, were rejected, company executives said.

Headlines: Ant Financial appoints Simon Hu as CEO, part of Alibaba's executive shuffle
Description: E-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd  and its fintech affiliate Ant Financial announced a string of top level executive changes on Thursday, amid an ongoing restructuring following the appointment of Daniel Zhang as chairman of Alibaba.

Headlines: Odebrecht offered Mexico $18 million to resolve graft cases: document
Description: Mexico this year rejected an offer by Brazilian construction firm Odebrecht SA [ODBES.UL] to pay $18 million and supply information related to graft cases, according to a document and a person with knowledge of the matter, the conglomerate's latest attempt to move past a major regional corruption scandal.

Headlines: Strong smartphone sales raise hopes of Samsung turnaround
Description: Strong sales of Samsung Electronics' Galaxy Note 10 smartphone series are limiting forecast profit falls at the South Korean tech giant, raising hopes it is getting back on a growth track after years of moribund sales.

Headlines: Majority of Americans favor wealth tax on very rich: Reuters/Ipsos poll
Description: The idea of imposing a wealth tax on the richest Americans has elicited sharply divergent views across a spectrum of politicians, with President Donald Trump branding it socialist and progressive Democratic presidential contenders Senators Elizabeth Warren and Bernie Sanders prominently endorsing it.

Headlines: UBS executives pledge $5 million of own cash to coronavirus fight
Description: Top managers at UBS  will each contribute the equivalent of three months' salary to fight the coronavirus, its chief executive Sergio Ermotti said on Thursday after the Swiss bank bowed to pressure to suspend its dividend.

Headlines: Wall Street drops after Fed chair dampens rate-cut hopes
Description: U.S. stocks ended lower on Wednesday and the S&P 500 snapped a three-day streak of record high closes as comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell appeared to dampen hopes the central bank could move later this year to cut interest rates.

Headlines: Volkswagen to recall 700,000 cars over roof lighting: trade magazine
Description: Volkswagen  has to recall about 700,000 Tiguan and Touran cars worldwide due to a possible lighting defect, German trade magazine Kfz-Betrieb reported on Monday.

Headlines: China's December property investment slows in sign of fatigue for key GDP driver
Description: Growth in property investment in China cooled to the second slowest pace in 2018 in December, adding to signs of a further slackening in the real estate market in a blow to a key driver economic growth.

Headlines: Delta, United poised for most new slots at Tokyo's Haneda airport
Description: Delta Air Lines and United Airlines are poised to win the most new daytime slots at Tokyo's Haneda International Airport in time for the 2020 Summer Olympics, according to a U.S. Department of Transportation statement on Thursday.

Headlines: Amazon extends work from home policy, still restricting travel
Description: Amazon.com Inc  has extended a work-from-home policy until Jan. 8 and is continuing to ask employees to defer all non-essential travel, a spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Oil hits 2019 high on U.S. plan to tighten squeeze on Iran
Description: Oil prices jumped more than 2 percent on Monday to a near six-month high, on growing concern about tight global supplies after the United States announced a further clampdown on Iranian oil exports.

Headlines: Apple, Qualcomm gird for next phase of patent battle after mixed U.S. rulings
Description: Split decisions on Tuesday by a U.S. government panel in  acrimonious patent disputes between iPhone-maker Apple and chip supplier Qualcomm left their battle lines largely unchanged ahead of a U.S Federal Trade Commission ruling and a major trial next month.

Headlines: Monte dei Paschi's bosses confident about turnaround plan: sources
Description: The top executives of bailed-out Italian bank Monte dei Paschi di Siena  told investors in London on Wednesday the bank is making progress with its turnaround plan, two fund managers who attended the meetings said.

Headlines: Australia tells Facebook and Google to commit to competition rules, or else
Description: Australia said on Thursday technology giants such as Facebook Inc  and Google  will have to agree to new rules to ensure they do not abuse their market power and damage competition, or the government will impose new controls on them.

Headlines: Chevron names Brazil chief to lead Venezuela operations after arrests
Description: (This version of the June 8 story corrects fourth paragraph to show La Rosa previously served as commercial manager in Venezuela, not country manager)

Headlines: Facebook's Zuckerberg unscathed by congressional grilling, stock rises
Description: Facebook Inc Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg fielded 10 hours of questions over two days from nearly 100 U.S. lawmakers and emerged largely unscathed and considerably richer.

Headlines: Ford, Jaguar slash thousands of jobs across Europe
Description: Ford  and Jaguar Land Rover unveiled sweeping job cuts across Europe on Thursday as carmakers struggle with a slump in demand for diesel vehicles, tougher emissions rules and a global economic slowdown led by China.

Headlines: U.S., China made 'some progress' on structural issues in trade talks: U.S. Chamber
Description: The United States and China made "some progress" in addressing differences over intellectual property rights and market access issues, but still have gaps in other structural issues, U.S. Chamber of Commerce officials briefed on the trade talks said on Thursday.

Headlines: Caution grips European stocks ahead of U.S. mid-term results
Description: European shares ended a choppy session in negative territory on Tuesday as investors punished companies like Zalando that missed expectations and remained cautious while waiting for the results of U.S. mid-term elections.

Headlines: U.S. commerce secretary, Chinese vice premier to hold dinner meeting on Sat: U.S. official
Description: U.S. Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross will have a dinner meeting with Chinese Vice Premier Liu He on Saturday evening at Beijing's Diaoyutai State Guest House, a U.S. government official said.

Headlines: Steve Cohen's venture firm invests in U.S. cybersecurity company
Description: Billionaire investor Steve Cohen's Point72 Ventures has invested in a U.S. cybersecurity firm that will provide a way to detect, alert, and protect against data- and identity-related attacks, according to one of the venture capital company's top officials.

Headlines: U.S. presidential candidate Warren calls on AT&T to reject plan she says will cost jobs
Description: U.S. presidential candidate Elizabeth Warren called on AT&T Inc to reject an activist investor plan she said would lead to job cuts, staking out a different position than President Donald Trump who has cheered the investor's involvement.

Headlines: Japan, South Korea raise stakes in dispute over forced labor
Description: Japan and South Korea raised the stakes on Tuesday in a dispute that threatens to disrupt global supplies of smartphones and chips, with South Korea denouncing Japanese reports it had transferred a sensitive chemical to North Korea.

Headlines: Cathay Pacific shares slide to nine-year low as data leak rattles investors
Description: Shares of Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd  slid nearly 7 percent to a nine-year low on Thursday after it said data of about 9.4 million passengers of Cathay and its unit, Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd, had been accessed without authorization.

Headlines: Facebook, Amazon and Alphabet take center stage on Wall Street
Description: The so-called FANG stocks take center stage on Wall Street this week, with Amazon , Alphabet  and Facebook  set to report as the S&P 500 approaches a record high.

Headlines: Calvin Klein owner PVH profit up 38 percent, forecast raised
Description: Apparel maker PVH Corp  reported a 38 percent rise in second-quarter profit on Wednesday and raised its earnings forecasts for the year, helped by higher sales of its Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger brands.

Headlines: Trump says doesn't want to talk to Xi, could even cut China ties
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump signaled a further deterioration of his relationship with China over the coronavirus outbreak, saying he has no interest in speaking to President Xi Jinping right now and going so far as to suggest he could even cut ties with the world's second largest economy.

Headlines: PSA Group may start production of Opel cars in Russia
Description: French carmaker PSA Group may begin assembling Opel cars at its Russian plant in Kaluga, the company said on Tuesday, as it reintroduces the brand to the country.

Headlines: Death of chairman adds to King Power uncertainty as Thai duty-free changes loom
Description: The death of Leicester City soccer club owner Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha adds to challenges his King Power International empire faces as its dominance of the lucrative Thai duty-free industry comes under scrutiny.

Headlines: Vivendi CEO denies company wants to call Telecom Italia shareholder meeting on board
Description: A report Vivendi  is thinking of calling a shareholder meeting at Telecom Italia  to appoint four more board members are off the mark, the French media group's CEO said.

Headlines: Timeline: Saudi Aramco's winding road to an IPO
Description: State-run oil giant Saudi Aramco has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at the top of its indicative range, making it the world's biggest flotation by raising more than Alibaba's  $25 billion listing in 2014.

Headlines: U.S., South Korea revise trade deal with quotas on Korean steel
Description: The United States and South Korea agreed to revise a trade pact sharply criticized by U.S. President Donald Trump, Seoul said on Monday, with U.S. automakers winning improved market access and Korean steelmakers hit with quotas but avoiding hefty tariffs.

Headlines: Instant View: S&P rises above 3,000 level for first time since March
Description: U.S. stocks rose above the 3,000 level for the first time since March 5 on Tuesday, continuing a rally that has pushed the benchmark index up nearly 35% from its March 23 closing low on hopes for a potential coronavirus vaccine and the reopening of businesses across the country.

Headlines: Mediobanca CEO expects second-tier banks to look at M&A in 2020
Description: Second-tier banks in Italy, Spain and possibly Germany are likely to consider mergers this year in a bid to boost returns which are insufficient to cover their cost of equity, the chief executive of investment bank Mediobanca said.

Headlines: Aeroplane parts maker FACC scouts for takeovers and ramps up Brexit production
Description: Austrian aeroplane parts maker FACC is ready to spend 500 million euros ($572 million) on acquisitions to make it less dependent on suppliers, add new technologies and strengthen its core business, its chief executive said.

Headlines: Canada's tourism industry 'deeply affected' by virus outbreak: minister
Description: The outbreak of the new coronavirus is hammering Canada's tourism industry, a senior government official said on Friday, as the number of visitors from China plummeted and after the cancellation of a major technology convention.

Headlines: World shares inch up on Wall Street; trade worries boost safety assets
Description: A gauge of global stocks eked out a gain as Wall Street closed higher on rises in financial and technology shares on Thursday, but U.S.-driven trade tensions continued to weigh on sentiment and boosted safety buying of Treasuries and German Bunds.

Headlines: Aramco trades below IPO price for first time, after OPEC pact unravels
Description: Shares of Saudi state oil company Aramco  slumped below their initial public offering (IPO) price on Sunday for the first time since they began trading in December, after OPEC's pact with Russia to restrict oil supplies fell apart on Friday.

Headlines: Steel, aluminum stocks gain as U.S. moves ahead with tariffs
Description: Shares of U.S. steel and aluminum producers gained on Thursday after the Trump administration moved ahead with tariffs on aluminum and steel imports from Canada, Mexico and the European Union, ending a two-month exemption.

Headlines: Gilead prices COVID-19 drug remdesivir at $2,340 per patient in developed nations
Description: Gilead Sciences Inc on Monday priced its COVID-19 antiviral remdesivir at $2,340 per patient for wealthier nations and agreed to send nearly all of its supply of the drug to the United States over the next three months.

Headlines: French 'AHTOP' tourism association urges France to act after Airbnb ruling
Description: France's 'AHTOP' tourism association urged the French government to take action after U.S. homesharing site Airbnb won its battle to remain exempt from onerous European property regulations.

Headlines: Limited engagement: Top funds backed gunmaker Ruger board despite no talks
Description: Funds run by BlackRock Inc  and Vanguard Group backed all  directors at gunmaker Sturm Ruger & Co Inc  despite the company's rare rejection of talks with the world's top asset managers, disclosures to regulators on Thursday showed.

Headlines: Trump's tariff ambush risks pushing Brazil closer to China
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump's surprise decision to slap metals tariffs on Brazil is a blow to President Jair Bolsonaro's aim of forging closer ties with Washington and could push Latin America's No. 1 economy closer to Trump's top trade foe - China.

Headlines: Mnuchin says small business rescue loans launch Friday, despite lender confusion
Description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said he was pressing ahead with the Friday launch of a $349 billion coronavirus rescue loan program for small businesses, after conceding to bank demands to fix aspects of the program that they said could cause participating lenders legal and financial risks.

Headlines: U.S. Treasury's Mnuchin: Revoking Boeing, Airbus licenses to sell jets to Iran
Description: Licenses for Boeing Co and Airbus to sell passenger jets to Iran will be revoked, U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Tuesday after President Donald Trump pulled the United States out of the 2015 Iran nuclear agreement.

Headlines: Britain's Big Four accountants could gain reprieve from audit reform
Description: Britain's business ministry will consult further on sweeping reforms of the audit market, it told Reuters, stopping short of legislation demanded by lawmakers.

Headlines: Renault convenes board to turn page on Ghosn era
Description: Renault  has called a board meeting to replace Chairman and Chief Executive Carlos Ghosn, in a move that may begin to ease tensions with alliance partner Nissan  in the wake of Ghosn's arrest in Japan for alleged financial misconduct.

Headlines: Nine state attorneys general back AT&T in Time Warner appeal
Description: A group of nine state attorneys general on Wednesday backed AT&T Inc  as the Justice Department asks a federal appeals court to reverse approval of the company's $85.4 billion acquisition of Time Warner Inc.

Headlines: How multi-strategy funds are faring as coronavirus slashes returns
Description: Just one of the world's biggest multi-strategy funds available to retail investors is in the black for the year after coronavirus panic saw markets fall across the board, data from Morningstar showed.

Headlines: Fed's Bullard considers current U.S. rate setting 'slightly restrictive'
Description: The U.S. Federal Reserve's interest rate increase in December likely tipped monetary policy into slightly restrictive territory, a step beyond the neutral level policymakers had hoped to hit, St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank President James Bullard said on Thursday.

Headlines: AirAsia X names new CEO to take over from co-founders
Description: Malaysia's long-haul budget carrier AirAsia X  on Thursday appointed Nadda Buranasiri as its new group chief executive officer to take over from its co-founders.

Headlines: Germany's Merck makes $5.9 billion counterbid for Versum
Description: German drugs and lab supplies maker Merck KGaA offered $5.9 billion, including debt, for Versum Materials, in a cash deal that tops an offer from U.S. rival Entegris, as both seek to boost their electrochemicals operations.

Headlines: Instant View: Fed's Powell sees more gradual rate hikes
Description: The Federal Reserve will likely need to keep raising interest rates to keep inflation under control, Fed Chairman Jerome Powell said in a speech on the economic outlook that did not address the economic risks of rising trade tensions.

Headlines: Nissan to set out survival plan after expected annual loss
Description: Nissan Motor Co  will unveil its plan to become a smaller, more cost-efficient automaker on Thursday as it looks to recover from four years of tumbling profits which are set to culminate in its first annual operating loss in 11 years.

Headlines: Trump agrees to help Mexico meet global oil cut target
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday he would help Mexico contribute to global oil output reductions, in a surprise move that could break an impasse among the world's major oil producers over cutbacks aimed at stabilizing crude prices.

Headlines: Honeywell beats quarterly profit estimates, raises 2019 forecast
Description: Honeywell International Inc  on Thursday reported a better-than-expected quarterly earnings and raised its full-year sales and profit forecasts, riding on higher demand for aircraft parts and spares, sending its shares up 1%.

Headlines: China's JD.com boss criticizes 'slackers' as company makes cuts
Description: Richard Liu, the founder of Chinese e-commerce giant JD.com Inc, has weighed in on an ongoing debate about the Chinese tech industry's grueling overtime work culture, lamenting that years of growth had increased the number of "slackers" in his firm who are not his "brothers."

Headlines: Unions urge Airbus to extend output freeze due to virus fears
Description: French unions are urging Airbus  to keep its French factories closed beyond March 23, when it plans to resume production after a four-day shutdown, raising questions over the knock-on impact on plants elsewhere in Europe.

Headlines: Papa John's Chairman John Schnatter resigns
Description: Pizza chain Papa John's International Inc  said on Wednesday its founder and former chief executive, John Schnatter, resigned as chairman of the board.

Headlines: Norwegian Air scraps 3,000 flights, plans layoffs due to coronavirus
Description: Norwegian Air  will lay off staff and cut around 3,000 flights as the spread of the new coronavirus outbreak sends shockwaves across the travel industry.

Headlines: Factbox: How we die: coronavirus in perspective
Description: As the new coronavirus spreads and worldwide deaths linked to it top 3,400, global alarm is growing and has caused everything from consumer runs on face masks to mass school closures.

Headlines: AT&T to launch wireless plans bundled with video after Time Warner win
Description: AT&T Inc  will launch two new unlimited wireless plans next week that will be bundled with a new video streaming service called WatchTV, in the company's first move to pair entertainment with phone service after closing its $85 billion acquisition of media company Time Warner Inc.

Headlines: Thyssenkrupp's elevator business gets at least 3 bidders: sources
Description: By Tom Käckenhoff, Christoph Steitz, Arno Schuetze and Edward Taylor

Headlines: Tesla, Elon Musk win dismissal of lawsuit over Model 3 production
Description: A federal judge in San Francisco dismissed for the second time a securities fraud lawsuit brought by Tesla Inc shareholders alleging that the company made misleading comments about the production status of its Model 3.

Headlines: Mexico to propose NAFTA renegotiator to lead WTO: sources
Description: Mexico is set to propose senior trade official Jesus Seade, who helped rework the North American Free Trade Agreement, as a candidate to be the next director-general of the World Trade Organization (WTO), sources said on Sunday.

Headlines: ArcelorMittal offers $2 billion of shares, convertibles at discount
Description: ArcelorMittal , the world's largest steelmaker, is issuing $2 billion of shares and convertible notes at a deep discount to accelerate debt reduction plans that have been slowed by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Headlines: Prominent investors stock up on eBay, then activists flex muscle
Description: EBay Inc.'s stock price slumped for most of last year but a number of prominent hedge funds were so convinced that change is on the horizon for the e-commerce company that they established new or added to existing positions in the last months of 2018.

Headlines: Brazil JBS workers catch COVID-19 in latest meat plant outbreak

Headlines: Tailored Brands may seek Chapter 11 protection if COVID effect continues
Description: Men's Wearhouse owner Tailored Brands Inc  said on Wednesday it may have to seek bankruptcy protection or discontinue operations, if the COVID-19 crisis continues to pummel sales.

Headlines: Bull market beliefs: Stock experts differ on market cycles
Description: As Wall Street prepares on Wednesday to celebrate the current U.S. bull stock market becoming the longest in history, some investors are keeping corks in their champagne bottles.

Headlines: U.S. insurers want taxpayers to back pandemic coverage for businesses

Headlines: Credit Suisse investigated by Geneva prosecutors in Turkish case

Description: China's coal output hit its highest in nine months in September, government data showed on Friday, boosted as new mining capacity started up in the country's northwest.

Headlines: Drugmakers Mylan, Pfizer delay merger due to coronavirus outbreak

Headlines: Campbell Soup offers to add two Third Point nominees to board

Description: A plunge in U.S. markets on Monday triggered a 15-minute trading halt in stocks after the S&P 500 fell 7% shortly after the market opened.

Description: Bombardier said it has resumed delivering subway cars to New York City Transit on Monday, spokesman Eric Prud'Homme said by email, after the agency halted deliveries last week because of performance problems.

Headlines: U.S. outlines strong support for self-driving cars at CES

Description: After a brutal meltdown, some investors have been wading back into U.S. stocks. But others are wary of another leg down as the coronavirus spreads and its economic impact is difficult to predict.

Headlines: New-look U.S. bank 'stress tests' may leave analysts guessing
Description: U.S. bank analysts have cleared their diaries on Thursday ahead of a long evening poring over results of the Federal Reserve's bank health checks, which have been upended this year by the coronavirus pandemic.

Headlines: Britain's 'Aramco' listing category attracts interest from a single firm
Description: Britain's markets watchdog has so far been contacted by only one company interested in taking advantage of a rule it introduced to attract state-owned firms like Saudi Aramco  to London, the regulator told Reuters without naming the firm.

Headlines: Disney must offer to buy all of Sky, Britain's takeover regulator rules
Description: Britain's takeover regulator said Walt Disney  must offer to buy all of Sky if it acquires Twenty-First Century Fox's 39 percent stake and if Rupert Murdoch's Fox is prevented from purchasing all of the European pay-TV company itself.

Headlines: Airbnb to report homeowners' income to Danish tax authorities
Description: Airbnb will automatically report homeowners' income to Danish tax authorities in what will be the first such agreement globally for the short-term rental service.

Headlines: Yemen Houthi drones, missiles defy years of Saudi air strikes

Headlines: China set to post slowest growth in 28 years in 2018, more stimulus seen
Description: China is expected to report on Monday that economic growth cooled to its slowest in 28 years in 2018 amid weakening domestic demand and bruising U.S. tariffs, adding pressure on Beijing to roll out more support measures to avert a sharper slowdown.

Headlines: Wall Street analysts bullish over Nike's digital growth, look past margin weakness

Headlines: Huawei set to announce lawsuit against U.S. as it seeks to strike back

Headlines: Microsoft hails revamped goggles as more immersive and easy to wear
Description: Microsoft unveiled the latest version of its HoloLens augmented reality headset on Sunday, promising wearers would feel more immersed in the augmented reality experience and more comfortable.

Headlines: Renault, Nissan boards get investigation updates before expected new Ghosn indictment
Description: The boards of Renault  and Japanese partner Nissan  met on Thursday for an update on ongoing investigations surrounding alleged financial misconduct by alliance boss Carlos Ghosn, both companies said.

Headlines: China says trade war to 'certainly' hurt U.S. exporters, create opportunities to others
Description: China is being forced to retaliate against the United States in their trade dispute, and U.S. exporters including suppliers of liquefied natural gas would "certainly" be hurt, said Chinese vice commerce minister Wang Shouwen.

Headlines: Daimler profits halve on diesel and restructuring charges
Description: Daimler  warned its earnings halved in 2019 and it faced further charges of up to 1.5 billion euros ($1.7 billion)related to diesel pollution, in the latest blow to the German luxury carmaker.

Headlines: Buffett appears to fault Trump, laments deals dearth in Berkshire letter
Description: Warren Buffett on Saturday appeared to fault U.S. President Donald Trump for taking too much credit for the nation's economic growth, while acknowledging that market conditions are making it tough for his Berkshire Hathaway Inc to find more big companies to buy.

Description: Facebook Inc's  Silicon Valley campus received the all-clear on Tuesday after fears that a package at its mail facility contained the nerve agent sarin.

Description: Tesla Inc  chief Elon Musk told employees on Monday the company was undergoing a "thorough reorganization" as it contends with production problems, senior staff departures and recent crashes involving its electric cars.

Description: Britain set out the type of deal it wants with the European Union on Monday, defining post-Brexit relations between the world's fifth largest economy and its biggest trading partner.

Description: The new boss of Britain's BT Group will give each employee 500 pounds ($641) worth of shares, at a total cost of 50 million pounds, in one of his first moves to drive better performance at the telecoms giant.

Description: A Tencent-led consortium is taking a 10% stake in Vivendi's Universal Music Group, valuing the music label that houses Lady Gaga and The Beatles at 30 billion euros ($34 billion) and giving the Chinese firm a global backstage pass.

Description: The world's rich nations face a double-whammy, with ageing populations meaning more retirees -- just as low and negative interest rates make it harder for pension funds to secure the investment returns needed to fill up their coffers.

Headlines: Apple in charts before second-quarter earnings
Description: Apple reports second-quarter results later on Tuesday, following warnings from some chipmakers who supply the world's biggest smartphone makers about demand for the iPhone and other top-end models.

Headlines: Collapsing bond yields push world stocks to new highs
Description: Government bonds held near multi-year lows on Thursday on bets the U.S. Federal Reserve would cut interest rates this month and that other major central banks would embrace looser monetary policy, pushing world stocks to new 18-month highs.

Headlines: China firmly opposes currency manipulator label: PBOC
Description: China firmly opposes a U.S. decision to label it a currency manipulator, its central bank said on Tuesday, adding that Beijing has not used and will not use the yuan to cope with trade frictions with the world's biggest economy.

Headlines: Tiffany sticks to 2019 targets, helped by e-commerce; shares rebound
Description: Luxury retailer Tiffany & Co said Friday it expected earnings growth to resume in the second half of the year, helped by a healthy e-commerce business, a forecast that allowed investors to look past slightly disappointing quarterly sales.

Headlines: Trump called Boeing CEO to inquire about 737 MAX production halt: sources
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump called Boeing  Chief Executive Dennis Muilenburg this week to ask about the status of 737 MAX production, two people briefed on the matter confirmed.

Headlines: Engie says to end engineering contracts in Iran by November
Description: French gas and power group Engie  said on Friday it would end its engineering contracts in Iran by November.

Headlines: U.S. new home sales tumble in March
Description: Sales of new U.S. single-family homes dropped by the most in more than 6-1/2 years in March and further declines are likely as the novel coronavirus outbreak batters the economy and throws millions of Americans out of work.

Headlines: Papa John’s taps investment banks amid pressure from founder: sources
Description: Papa John’s International Inc , the world’s third-largest pizza delivery company, has hired Bank of America Corp  and Lazard Ltd  to help find ways to stabilize the restaurant chain, which has come under pressure from its founder John Schnatter, people familiar with the matter said on Friday.

Headlines: Turkey, trade worries hit Wall Street
Description: U.S. stock indexes fell sharply on Wednesday, hurt by concerns over a stronger dollar and Turkey's currency crisis, as well as over the trade tensions with U.S. trading partners that have dominated the first half of 2018.

Headlines: U.S. economy expands modestly but trade tensions weigh, Fed survey shows
Description: The U.S. economy expanded at a modest pace through the final six weeks of 2019 but uncertainty over U.S. trade policy continued to hurt firms, a survey conducted by the Federal Reserve said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Softbank pushes link-ups as insurance strategy takes shape
Description: Softbank's Vision Fund plans to pump more money into insurance, a sector it sees as both ripe for disruption and a potential booster for its bigger bets in cars, health and financial services, a Vision Fund executive told Reuters.

Headlines: Wall St. rallies on hopes of U.S. rate cut, trade progress
Description: Wall Street's major indexes charged higher on Friday, as sharply slowing U.S. job growth boosted hopes for Federal Reserve interest rate cuts while optimism about potential progress in U.S. trade fights with China and Mexico added to risk appetites.

Headlines: ECB weighs investigating Deutsche Bank over alleged unauthorized bond purchases: sources
Description: The European Central Bank is examining whether to open a formal investigation into Deutsche Bank  for allegedly buying some of its own securities without authorization, two people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Huge, pricey trucks haul jobs and profits for the Detroit Three
Description: Mickey McMaster is on his 12th pickup truck.

Headlines: Mylan offers concessions to address EU concerns about Pfizer deal
Description: Generic drugmaker Mylan NV  has offered concessions to address European Union antitrust concerns about its bid for Pfizer's  off-patent branded drugs business Upjohn, a filing on the European Commission site showed on Monday.

Headlines: Wall Street ekes out gains ahead of Singapore summit
Description: All three major U.S. stock indexes closed slightly higher on Monday as investors eyed the looming United States-North Korea summit on Tuesday in Singapore while shrugging off the weekend's factious meeting of the Group of Seven nations.

Headlines: France says Ghosn case not problem for Renault stability
Description: The arrest of Renault  CEO Carlos Ghosn and his imminent removal from the board of Nissan Motor Co.  does not pose a threat to the stability or survival of the French carmaker, France's finance minister said on Monday.

Headlines: Carrefour mounts shields for French cashiers in coronavirus crisis
Description: Carrefour  began putting up protective barriers for cashiers in its French supermarkets on Monday, as it beefs up sanitary measures and looks to keep business flowing as France shuts down other sectors to fight the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: Shoemaker Vans treads warily as China fumes over Hong Kong protests
Description: U.S. sports brand Vans has removed "a small number" of submissions in a sneaker design competition including one apparently giving a shout out to Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, as companies weigh the risks of angering China.

Headlines: 3M sues five vendors for attempting to sell nonexistent N95 respirators
Description: Industrial conglomerate 3M Co said on Friday it sued five vendors for allegedly attempting to target government officials with fraudulent offers to sell billions of nonexistent N95 respirators.

Headlines: JPMorgan Chase will invest $125 million in programs to encourage people to save money
Description: JPMorgan Chase & Co will provide $125 million over the next five years to nonprofit groups in the United States and abroad that help people save, pay down debt and improve their credit scores, the bank said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Judges named to hear government's appeal of AT&T Time Warner deal approval
Description: A panel of three federal appeals court judges named by former Presidents Ronald Reagan, Bill Clinton and Barack Obama will hear the Justice Department's appeal of a ruling allowing AT&T Inc to acquire Time Warner, court records show.

Headlines: Largest asset manager wins backing for jumbo board
Description: BlackRock Inc  said all of its 16 director nominees received strong investor support at its annual meeting on Thursday, at which Chief Executive Laurence Fink defended the size of the company's large board.

Headlines: Zoom shares slip over security concerns, rising competition
Description: Shares of Zoom Video Communications Inc  fell 8% on Monday, adding to their sharp declines in the past few days, as the video conferencing app battles privacy concerns and increased competition from deep-pocketed rivals.

Headlines: Trump to meet with Chinese Vice Premier Liu He at 2:45 p.m. EDT/1845 GMT Friday
Description: President Donald Trump will meet with Chinese Vice Premier Liu He at 2:45 p.m. EDT/1845 GMT on Friday as the world's two biggest economies try to reach a trade agreement, the White House said.

Headlines: Powell: Fed to act as appropriate to keep expansion going
Description: The U.S. economy is in a "favorable place" and the Federal Reserve will "act as appropriate" to keep the current economic expansion on track, Fed chair Jerome Powell said on Friday in remarks that gave few clues about whether the central bank will cut interest rates at its next meeting or not.

Headlines: OPEC's Barkindo says OPEC, non-OPEC agreement rescued oil industry
Description: OPEC Secretary-General Mohammad Barkindo said on Friday members of the oil producers group were friends of the United States and have a vested interest in its growth and prosperity.

Headlines: Wall Street ends flat amid rate hopes, tech declines
Description: U.S. stocks ended flat on Monday as increased expectations of stimulus from central banks around the world were offset by losses in technology and healthcare shares.

Headlines: Exclusive: PetroChina to drop PDVSA as partner in refinery project - sources
Description: PetroChina Co plans to drop Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) as a partner in a planned $10 billion oil refinery and petrochemical project in southern China, said three sources familiar with the matter this week.

Headlines: Colombian proposal to ditch NY coffee price may send buyers elsewhere
Description: A proposal by Colombian coffee growers' federation that producer countries sell their high-quality harvests untethered from the New York market price could encourage buyers to look for alternative providers, importers and exporters said.

Headlines: Geneva motor show postponed until 2022: organizers
Description: The organizers of the Geneva International Motor Show said on Monday that they would not organize the event in 2021.

Headlines: Oil sinks as manufacturing data feeds global economy worries
Description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday, with U.S. crude futures down 2% after manufacturing data raised concerns about a weakening global economy, while the U.S.-China trade dispute continued to drag on investor sentiment.

Headlines: Jury says J&J must pay $8 billion in case over male breast growth linked to Risperdal
Description: Johnson & Johnson must pay $8 billion in punitive damages to a man who previously won $680,000 over his claims that it failed to warn that young men using its antipsychotic drug Risperdal could grow breasts, a Philadelphia jury said on Tuesday.

Headlines: U.S. Transportation Dept. IG to audit FAA pilot training requirements after Boeing 737 MAX crashes
Description: The U.S. Transportation Department's Office of Inspector General said on Monday it will audit Federal Aviation Administration pilot training requirements for U.S. and foreign air carriers after two deadly crashes of Boeing's  737 MAX.

Headlines: World Bank shareholders back $13 billion capital increase
Description: The World Bank's shareholders on Saturday endorsed a $13 billion paid-in capital increase that will boost China's shareholding but bring lending reforms that will raise borrowing costs for  higher-middle-income countries, including China.

Headlines: Russia cut oil output by 278,000 bpd in June: Ifax
Description: Russia cut its oil output in June by an average of 278,000 barrels per day from levels seen last October, Interfax news agency cited Russian Energy Minister Alexander Novak as saying on Monday.

Headlines: FAA chief to meet with Boeing officials, test 737 MAX simulator
Description: New Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) chief Stephen Dickson plans to fly to Seattle this week to fly "newly configured" Boeing 737 MAX software in a simulator and will visit with Boeing  officials, the agency said Monday.

Headlines: Bank of America restricts trading in penny stocks
Description: Bank of America  is placing trading restrictions on penny stocks as part of a policy change aimed at shielding clients from risky assets, the Wall Street bank said on Friday.

Headlines: ABB's Voser battles headwinds as he pursues overhaul
Description: ABB  is pressing ahead with a review of its underperforming businesses and expects a turbulent 2019 amid a slowdown in some markets and China-U.S. trade tensions, Chairman and interim Chief Executive Peter Voser told Reuters.

Headlines: Bombardier to deliver handful of Global 7500 jets in first half 2019
Description: Bombardier Inc, the Canadian train and plane maker, will deliver a handful of its new flagship Global 7500 business jets to customers in the first half of 2019, with the remaining 10-15 deliveries expected in the second half, its chief financial officer said on Wednesday.

Headlines: Trump says OPEC can step up output after Iran waivers
Description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday that Saudi Arabia and other OPEC nations could "more than make up" for any drop in Iranian oil supplies to global markets now that his administration has decided to end waivers that allowed some nations to buy Iranian oil without facing U.S. sanctions.

Headlines: GE's demolished dividend shreds shareholders' safety net
Description: General Electric Co shareholders were dealt yet another blow on Tuesday.

Headlines: Swiss seek quick talks with Malaysia on 1MDB investigation
Description: Swiss federal prosecutors are seeking quick talks with Malaysian counterparts on how to press forward with an investigation of suspected corruption surrounding scandal-hit sovereign wealth fund 1MDB, the Swiss attorney general's office said on Tuesday.

Headlines: Canadian court bail hearing for Huawei CFO adjourned until Monday
Description: A bail hearing for the chief financial officer of China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd was adjourned until Monday, after

Headlines: Top shareholder's candidate for chairman elected to Danske Bank board
Description: Danske Bank  shareholders elected Karsten Dybvad, who was proposed by top shareholder A. P. Moller Holding as the bank's new chairman, to the board at an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Friday.

Headlines: EU leaders tell social networks to guarantee users' privacy
Description: EU leaders on Thursday urged social networks to guarantee transparent practices and fully protect personal information as pressure piled on Facebook after allegations that data from 50 million of its users was mishandled.

Headlines: Thomson Reuters to move forex derivatives to Dublin due to Brexit
Description: Thomson Reuters Corp said on Tuesday it would transfer its $300 billion-a-day foreign exchange derivatives trading business to Dublin from London ahead of Britain's departure from the European Union next year.

Headlines: Factbox: Airlines suspend flights due to coronavirus outbreak
Description: Airlines across the globe have suspended flights or modified services in response to the coronavirus outbreak.

Headlines: JPMorgan trades banker offices for shared desks
Description: NEW YORK - JPMorgan Chase & Co is tearing down walls and moving its San Francisco investment bankers onto "hot desks," a space-saving layout that has long been a fixture at tech companies, while redesigning offices in Dallas and other cities.

Headlines: Analyst view: Fed's day two of cash injection into U.S. banking system
Description: As if the U.S. Federal Reserve didn't already have enough on its plate heading into its meeting on interest rates this week, chaos deep inside the plumbing of the U.S. financial system has thrown policymakers an unexpected curve ball.

Headlines: APEC fails to live up to its name amid U.S., China acrimony
Description: The C in APEC stands for Cooperation. But when the two biggest members are fighting a trade war and using the forum to attack each other's policies, it was always going to be hard work delivering on that.

Headlines: Czech cyber watchdog says its Huawei warning took U.S. by surprise
Description: The Czech cyber-security watchdog was not pressured by the United States or anyone else into issuing its warning about the possible security risks posed by Chinese telecoms equipment maker Huawei, Prague's cyber attache to Washington told Reuters.
